sections.title: Updates from Prior Versions (v1–v8 change log)
sections.text:
0. UPDATES FROM PRIOR VERSIONS
The New York State Office of Health Insurance Programs (OHIP) seeks to maintain an up-to-date SCN Operations
Manual to guide SCNs and other stakeholders during the lifetime of the SCN Program. The original SCN
Operations Manual v1 was released on August 9, 2024, and additional versions have been released since the
original version 1. Revisions to the Manual may be required as OHIP seeks to provide additional details and
clarification, or due to changes in guidance as a result of learnings from program implementation. Additional
versions will be made available by OHIP as needed.
A summary of changes for each version is below.
   •   ORIGINAL – Version 1 (August 9, 2024): First release of OHIP’s operational guidance for the SCN
       Program
   •   Version 2 (October 29, 2024): Includes additional details and clarifications to overall SCN guidance.
       Larger additions and revisions include (not exhaustive):
           • SCN Infrastructure
                   ▪ New guidance on HRSN service provider and ecosystem partner complaints
                   ▪ Clarifications on use of infrastructure funding for capacity building
                   ▪ Updates to SCN public website requirements
                   ▪ New section on public-facing materials related to SCN program
           • Care Delivery Approach
                   ▪ New guidance regarding identification of member major life events
                   ▪ New guidance on requirements for Social Care Navigation to be reimbursed using
                       Waiver funds
                   ▪ Updates to Eligibility Assessment process (e.g., requirement to gather member consent,
                       requirement to answer data fields for all questions)
                   ▪ Revised guidance on implications of changes in member Medicaid coverage
                   ▪ New section on determining member program eligibility through provider attestation
                       and/or member documentation/attestation
                   ▪ Additional guidance and details for individual Enhanced HRSN Services added for
                       services including Home Accessibility / Safety Modification, Home Remediation, Asthma
                       Remediation, Medical Respite, Housing Transition and Navigation, and Transportation
                       Services
           • Performance
                   ▪ Updated dates for major report submissions
                   ▪ New section on member complaints and reportable incidents to replace previous
                       guidance
           • Payments
                   ▪ Clarified guidance on use of Infrastructure funding
                   ▪ Updated guidance for HRSN fee schedule and Enhanced HRSN Service rate types
           • Contract Requirements
                   ▪ New guidance regarding OHIP’s SCN Conflict of Interest (COI) Plan requirement
                   ▪ Clarification on guidance for Health Homes contracting into the SCN
[[p.6]]
            •   Data Governance, Privacy, and Security
                   ▪ Updated dates for data and security deliverables
   •   Version 3 (December 13, 2024): Includes additional details and clarifications to SCN guidance. Larger
       additions and revisions include (not exhaustive):
          • SCN Infrastructure
                   ▪ Added additional detail on coding granularly and SCN IT platform functionality to enable
                       Eligibility Assessment
          • Care Delivery Approach
                   ▪ Added member demographic questions to questions to be asked during Screening
                       instead of Eligibility Assessment
                   ▪ Provided additional detail on how Social Care Navigators should conduct Eligibility
                       Assessments, particularly sources of data for determining member Medicaid Managed
                       Care (MMC) enrollment
                   ▪ Provided additional guidance on how Social Care Navigators should take into account
                       households when navigating eligible members to Enhanced HRSN services
                   ▪ Added considerations for criminal justice-involved adults and justice-involved youth
                   ▪ Added specific timing for sharing of monthly Enhanced Services Member File (ESMF)
                   ▪ Updated Enhanced Population descriptions, clinical criteria, and Social Risk Factors per
                       CMS
                   ▪ Provided additional detail on eligibility verification pathways, including suggested script
                       for member attestation and details on provider attestation workflow
                   ▪ Clarified workflows for Home Remediation and Nutrition services
          • Performance
                   ▪ Adjusted guidance for Network Composition Report required components
                   ▪ Clarified guidance for handling of and reporting requirements for member complaints
          • Payments
                   ▪ Added additional guidance on reimbursement of services delivered by HRSN service
                       providers within the SCN
          • Data Governance, Privacy, and Security
                   ▪ Clarified HITRUST certification requirements for SCN IT environments
                   ▪ Updated guidance for Summary of Privacy & Security requirements and deliverables
   •   Version 4 (March 21, 2025): Includes additional details and clarifications to SCN guidance. Larger
       additions and revisions include (not exhaustive):
          ○ SCN Infrastructure
                   ▪ Clarified eligibility for and intended use of community-based organization (CBO)
                       capacity building funds
                   ▪ Provided additional detail on automated IT Platform logic expected to guide Social Care
                       Navigators during Eligibility Assessment
          • Care Delivery Approach
                   ▪ Included additional considerations for youth and interpersonal safety (IPS) questions
                       asked during Screening
[[p.7]]
                   ▪   Provided additional detail on how Social Care Navigators should perform Eligibility
                       Assessments, including when to collect documentation for verification of Social Risk
                       Factors
                    ▪ Clarified household guidance for Social Care Navigators, including how Social Care
                       Navigators should approach select services that may scale for multiple members within
                       the same household
                    ▪ Added guidance on youth residing in multiple households
                    ▪ Updated guidance for Social Care Navigators when members move across regions,
                       including process to update member address
                    ▪ Provided additional detail on expected components of Social Care Plans, including
                       technical requirement for platform vendors to generate a singular, comprehensive view
                       of a member’s Social Care Plan
                    ▪ Updated workflows for 2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications, 2.2 Home
                       Remediation Service, and 2.3 Asthma Remediation (including service limitations and
                       restrictions and allowable providers)
                    ▪ Clarified workflows for other Housing, Nutrition, and Transportation Services
                    ▪ Added additional guidance for Social Care Navigators on how to approach members that
                       are already receiving potentially duplicative services
            •   Performance
                    ▪ Provided additional detail on requirements for Infrastructure Cost Report and Quarterly
                       Member Complaints Report
            •   Payments
                    ▪ Clarified requirements for HRSN service providers to receive reimbursement
                    ▪ Clarified how HRSN service providers may braid funding sources to serve Medicaid
                       members
                    ▪ Clarified how time spent on coordination should be billed for different services
            •   Contract Requirements
                    ▪ Added additional detail around expectations for conflict of interest (COI) plans
                    ▪ Clarified how and when SCN Lead Entities can contract with Independent Practice
                       Associations (IPAs) and Office of Mental Health (OMH) facilities
            •   Data Governance, Privacy and Security
                    ▪ Added new Security and Privacy Section 10. OHIP Security and Privacy Requirements
                       including the removal of HITRUST requirements
            •   Fee Schedule
                    ▪ Added new Section 11. Fee Schedule with service-level detail from the HRSN fee
                       schedule
   •   Version 5 (August 1, 2025): Includes additional details and clarifications to SCN guidance. Larger
       additions and revisions include (not exhaustive):
          • SCN Infrastructure
                   ▪ Capacity funding: Provided additional clarity on allowable uses of capacity building
                       funding
                   ▪ SCN websites: Clarified expectations for SCN public websites (e.g., including Enhanced
                       Population criteria)
[[p.8]]
                    ▪  MEVS integration: Added additional detail on expectations for SCN IT Platforms to
                       integrate with MEVS
            •   Care Delivery Approach
                    ▪ Screening: Clarified definition of a complete Screening and requirements for
                       reimbursement
                    ▪ Service re-authorization: Specified guidance and processes for service re-authorization,
                       including Navigator workflows and clarifications on the duration of eligibility for relevant
                       services
                    ▪ Potentially duplicative services: Clarified guidance on potentially duplicative services
                       (e.g., guidance for Social Care Navigators to coordinate with MCO case managers,
                       guidance on Healthy Homes services)
                    ▪ Enhanced HRSN services: Provided additional detail on housing services, including
                       clarifications on QA inspections, Dwelling Assessments, and bid solicitations
                    ▪ Services for members in the same household: Clarified expectations for providing
                       services to members within households (e.g., criteria for a member to qualify for
                       household-level nutrition support, household billing guidelines for utility services)
                    ▪ Congestion pricing: Added new guidelines for congestion pricing tolls incurred as part of
                       private transportation services
                    ▪ Foster care: Added additional guidance on provision of HRSN services to children in
                       foster care and transitioning out of foster care
                    ▪ Member experience survey: Clarified expectations for SCN-administered member
                       experience survey
            •   Data Governance, Privacy, and Security
                    ▪ Quarterly POA&M and Quarterly Names List (QNL) Requirements: Clarified activities
                       for SCN Lead Entities to support oversight and compliance within Medicaid DUA and
                       privacy/security protocols
            •   Fee Schedule
                    ▪ Harmonized guidance to align with Fee Schedule v4 (released on 6/16/2025) and Fee
                       Schedule v5 (released on 8/1/2025)
                    ▪ Congestion pricing: Added new modifiers related to congestion pricing
   •   Version 6 (November 3, 2025): Includes additional details and clarifications to SCN guidance. Larger
       additions and revisions include (not exhaustive):
          • SCN Infrastructure
                   ▪ SCN IT Platform Requirements: Added requirement that SCN IT platforms must retain
                       all historical member data
                   ▪ SCN Public Website: Added best practices for self-screening tools
          • Care Delivery Approach
                   ▪ Eligibility Assessment: Added guidance on service duration pauses, expectations for
                       Social Care Navigator outreach to members, definition of a “complete” EA, new
                       guidance on what Social Care Navigators should do if unmet needs during EA differ from
                       initial screening, guidance for additional household members for Nutrition services, and
                       additional guidance for criminal justice-involved individuals
                   ▪ SCN Referrals: Clarified guidance on referral workflows
[[p.9]]
                    ▪  Service Re-authorization: Clarified that a new referral must be created for service re-
                       authorizations
                    ▪ Social Care Plan: Added requirements for which care plan elements should be
                       populated automatically or manually within SCN IT Platforms
                    ▪ HRSN Services: Clarified nature of 6-month service duration, which housing
                       modification services are considered “invasive”, updated guidance on bids required for
                       home modifications, and added guidance on if member elects to change type of
                       Nutrition service
                    ▪ Attestation: Added guidance that MCOs can provide written attestation in lieu of
                       providers; clarified that provider attestations are valid for 1 year and only one method is
                       required to validate member’s eligibility
            •   Performance
                    ▪ Member Satisfaction: Added additional guidance on requirements for member
                       experience surveys administered by SCN Lead Entities and termination of member
                       services
            •   Payments
                    ▪ PMPM Payments: Added additional details on PMPM administration and reconciliation
                       processes
            •   Contract Requirements
                    ▪ SCN Medicaid Billing Social Care Provider Designation and Enrollment: Clarified that
                       SCN Lead Entities are permitted to subcontract with vendors for select support
                    ▪ SCN Contract Requirements with HRSN Service Providers and Other Entities: Provided
                       additional guidance on HRSN service providers, Certified Community Behavioral Health
                       Clinics (CCBHCs) and Care Coordination Organizations (CCOs)
            •   Fee Schedule
                    ▪ Harmonized guidance to align with Fee Schedule v6 (released on 10/31/2025)
                    ▪ Nutrition: Clarified existing guidance; added household service codes and modifiers for
                       Nutrition services
                    ▪ Congestion pricing: Removed U/U modifiers
   •   Version 7 (January 31, 2026): Includes additional details and clarifications on SCN guidance. Larger
       additions and revisions include (non-exhaustive):
          • Care Delivery Approach
                   ▪ MLTCP/MAP members eligibility for nutrition and housing services: Clarified that
                       MLTCP/MAP members are eligible to receive 3.5 Cooking Supplies and that need for
                       housing services can be addressed with member verbal attestation (vs. only through
                       confirmation by MTLCP/MAP plan)
                   ▪ ESMF services data: For duplicative services, adjusted guidance to treat “U” (unknown)
                       values in the ESMF similar to “N” (no) values if member verbally attests to not being
                       enrolled in the program
                   ▪ Eligibility Assessment:
                             • Clarified guidance that Navigators must check for service duplication, but can
                                  refer to other services (that don’t require duplication checks) in the meantime
                             • Clarified circumstances under which a re-screening may be billed upon
                                  discovery of changed screening answers during Eligibility Assessment
[[p.10]]
                              •   Created guidance that Navigators may contact a Health Home care manager
                                  for confirmation (verbal, digital, written) that member is enrolled in a Health
                                  Home
                              • Clarified guidance on use of concurrent claim modifier when billing for same-
                                  day services to children living in multiple households
                    ▪ Service duplication check workflow: Clarified guidance that Navigators can outreach to
                       other programs and MCO contacts for service duplication checks at the end of the EA
                       and bill time under Enhanced Care Management
                    ▪ Provider Attestation: Added guidance to allow for electronic provider signatures (e.g.,
                       Docusign)
                    ▪ Medicaid Redesign Team Housing: Added Medicaid Redesign Team
                       (MRT) housing providers to Partnerships section and clarified MRT provider
                       reimbursement
                    ▪ Clinical Criteria: Clarified the clinical criteria for 2.4 Medical Respite and 3.2
                       Medically Tailored Meals
                    ▪ Rent/Temporary Housing: Clarified guidance that members should be placed in rental
                       units that are financially sustainable for the member beyond the HRSN service duration
                    ▪ Uncontrolled Asthma ESMF indicator: Clarified that ESMF indicator for
                       “Uncontrolled Asthma” meets clinical criteria to be eligible for a referral to 2.2 Asthma
                       Remediation, 2.2a Home Remediation: Mold and Pest Remediation, and 2.2b Home
                       Remediation: Ventilation Improving Systems without further documentation necessary
                    ▪ Home Remediation referrals for members receiving Asthma
                       Remediation services: Clarified that members with Asthma Remediation referrals are
                       eligible for 2.2a Home Remediation: Mold and Pest Remediation and 2.2b Home
                       Remediation: Ventilation Improving Systems without provider attestation
                    ▪ Billing for housing coordination: Clarified billing guidance on member-facing and non-
                       member facing time spent on coordinating housing services under 2.7 Pre-tenancy
                       Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services, 2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation
                       Services, and Enhanced Care Management
                    ▪ Transportation reimbursement: Clarified guidance that Transportation Services are only
                       reimbursable for actual services rendered to the member and are not reimbursable
                       when a member fails to show up for an appointment
                    ▪ Off platform screening: Clarified off platform screening section to enhance existing
                       guidance (corresponds to 1-pager on NYeC website)
            •   Performance
                    ▪ Member Experience Survey: Added the member experience survey to required
                       quarterly reporting
                    ▪ CBO Feedback: Added guidance for SCN LEs to gather CBO feedback annually
                    ▪ Operational Indicator Survey: Clarified guidance on submission requirements and
                       cadence for the operational indicator survey (replaces Monthly Horizon Report)
            •   Payments
                    ▪ Same day services: Clarified billing guidance for situations when a member receives a
                       same service, same day, by same rendering provider
[[p.11]]
                    ▪  Contract requirements: Clarified that outpatient Article 16 OPWDD and Article 32
                       OASAS providers may contract with SCN LEs and receive reimbursement for Screening
                       and Navigation
            •   Data Governance, Privacy, and Security
                    ▪ SCN referral tracking: Removed outdated guidance on SNOMED-CT referral codes
            •   Fee Schedule
                    ▪ L1 Units: Increased the maximum annual 1.1 Navigation Services units from 8 to
                       16 units
                    ▪ Broker’s fees: Adjusted guidance that CTS Broker’s Fees only apply to Long
                       Island SCN region after the NYC passage of the FARE Act
                    ▪ Asthma Self-Management Education: Adjusted guidance to allow virtual video calls
                       for the initial visit for 2.3a Asthma Self-Management Education (ASME)
                    ▪ Housing Services: Updated caps for 2.5 Rent / Temporary Housing and 2.8a Community
                       Transitional Supports (CTS) to 2026 HUD Fair Market Rents

Version 8 (May 1, 2026): Includes additional details and clarifications on SCN guidance. Larger additions and
revisions include (non-exhaustive):
             • Care Delivery Approach
                     ▪ Verbal and email attestations: Provided flexibility for MCOs and Health Homes to attest
                        to a member’s eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services using verbal attestation, HIPAA
                        compliant email confirmation, care coordination notes in the SCN IT Platform, or
                        Provider Attestion form. Allowed flexibility for other providers to attest to a member’s
                        eligibility criteria through HIPAA compliant email confirmation or Provider Attestation
                        form
                     ▪ Eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services: Updated eligibility determination pathways for
                        each Enhanced Population and Enhanced HRSN Service (Table 5-15)
                     ▪ Additional non-invasive services: Expanded non-invasive measures list to include non-
                        invasive deep cleaning prior to 2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications, 2.2a
                        Mold and Pest Remediation, 2.2b Ventilation Improving Systems or 2.3 Asthma
                        Remediation.
                     ▪ Non-invasive measures provided by ASME providers: Clarified that ASME providers
                        may provide non-invasive Asthma Remediation services if needed prior to SOW
                     ▪ MRT and ESSHI provider guidance: Updated guidance to include expectations that SCNs
                        will initiate contracting with Medicaid Redesign Team (MRT) Supportive Housing
                        subcontractors and Empire State Support Housing Initiative (ESSHI) providers
                     ▪ Enhanced Population status on ESMF: Clarified that Navigators do not need to ask the
                        member for further support to verify their “yes” enhanced population or clinical criteria
                        status as noted in the ESMF
                     ▪ Health Care Provider capacity funding: Added guidance on capacity building funds for
                        Health Care and Behavioral Health Care Providers to hire Social Care Navigators to
                        screen, assess, and refer members to HRSN Services
                     ▪ Social Care navigation billing: Clarified that Social Care Navigation is inclusive of
                        member-facing and non-member-facing coordination
[[p.12]]
                    ▪  Members experiencing interpersonal violence: Clarified that members experiencing
                       interpersonal violence should be prioritized and navigated to services as close to same
                       day of the eligibility assessment as possible
                    ▪ Temporary hotel stays for members with IPV: Expanded hotel/motel stay coverage to
                       members experiencing interpersonal violence so long as the Social Care Navigator,
                       housing provider, and member is developing a permanent, long-term housing or
                       transitional housing plan in parallel
                    ▪ “Completing” referrals for SNOMED code clarity: Added guidance that L1 and L2
                       services should be marked as “completed” by Navigators to ensure data is accurate
                       when pulling SNOMED codes
            •   Performance
                    ▪ Infrastructure Cost Report: Updated reporting cadence to reflect new monthly
                       reporting requirement
                    ▪ Infrastructure funding: Updated percentage of infrastructure funds tied to required
                       reporting and performance in PY 2 Q4
                             • Updated required reporting percentages from 85% to 80%
                             • Updated performance percentage from 10% to 15%

            •   Payments
                    ▪ HRSN Service Provider invoicing: Added guidance that HRSN Service Providers must
                       submit invoices no later than 5 business days after the service delivery date
                    ▪ SCN claim submission: Shifted requirement for SCNs to submit all claims to MCOs no
                       later than 10 business days from payment date
            •   Data Governance, Privacy, and Security
                    ▪ N/A
            •   Fee Schedule
                    ▪ Alignment with April 1, 2026 Release:
                              • Made updates to program-level caps (e.g., CTS Brokers Fee, Cooking Supplies
                                  and Transportation) to align with the HRSN Fee Schedule Version 8 released
                                  on April 1, 2026
                              • Removed coverage of broker’s fees from Manhattan, Bronx, Brooklyn,
                                  Queens, Staten Island in response to legislative changes in New York City and
                                  maintains coverage for Long Island

sections.title: Glossary of Common Terms
sections.text:
1. GLOSSARY OF COMMON TERMS

 Term                    Definition and term details
 Accountable Health      Standard New York Health Equity Reform (NYHER) HRSN assessment instrument
 Communities (AHC)       used to assess unmet HRSN needs
 Health-Related Social
 Need (HRSN) Screening
 Tool
 Community based         501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) non-profit community focused organization that provides
 organization (CBO)      HRSN services directly to members

                         CBOs may or may not bill Medicaid within their organization. CBOs may contract
                         with Social Care Network (SCN) Lead Entities to become part of a SCN.

                         (See Roles and responsibilities of entities within the Social Care Network and
                         broader ecosystem for more information)
 Clinical Criteria       The set of clinical criteria which renders a Medicaid Managed Care member
                         eligible for a specific Enhanced HRSN Service (e.g., Asthma Remediation)

                         Member must demonstrate medical necessity for individual Enhanced Services
                         and criteria is located within the Enhanced Services Member File

                         (See Clinical Criteria for more information)
 Data and Systems        An implementation guide developed by OHIP to provide member enrollment and
 Implementation Guide    population identification, HRSN billing, claims, and data management guidance for
 (DSIG)                  the successful implementation of the NYHER Program

                         Note: There are 2 versions of the DSIG tailored to SCN Lead Entity and MCO
                         audiences
 Detailed Business       Comprehensive definitions of metrics contained in performance management
 Requirements (DBRs)     reports, including, specific inputs and calculations required to measure those
                         outcomes (e.g., numerators, denominators)
 Ecosystem partners      Entities not contracted into the SCN but that may collaborate with the SCN,
                         including but not limited to managed care organizations (MCOs), local agencies /
                         departments, and health care providers, inclusive of behavioral health and
                         primary care providers, that may work with SCN but are not formally part of the
                         Network

                         (See Roles and responsibilities of entities within the Social Care Network and
                         broader ecosystem for more information)
[[p.14]]
 Term                     Definition and term details
 Eligibility Assessment   Assessment of a member’s eligibility for NYHER-financed Enhanced HRSN Services
                          conducted by a Social Care Navigator. Eligibility is based on criteria defined by the
                          Office of Health Insurance Programs (OHIP). This assessment takes place after
                          Screening and before service delivery in the NYHER process

                          (See Eligibility Assessment for more information)
 Enhanced Health-         Services reimbursed by OHIP for eligible Medicaid Managed Care members
 Related Social Need
 (HRSN) Services          Services include Care Management, Housing, Nutrition, and Transportation

 Enhanced Services        The Enhanced Services Member File indicates a Medicaid Managed Care
 Member File (ESMF)       member’s potential eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services based on clinical criteria
                          listed within this document in addition to member information obtained during
                          the Eligibility Assessment. Social Care Navigators must collectively use this
                          information to determine which Enhanced HRSN Services a member is eligible for
                          during the Eligibility Assessment. The file pathway for the Enhanced Services
                          Member File is from the MCO to New York eHealth Collaborative (NYeC)/
                          Statewide Health Information Network for New York (SHIN-NY) then QEs and
                          finally to the SCNs. The Enhanced Services Member File will be sent on a monthly
                          basis
 ePACES                   Electronic Provider Assisted Claim Entry System (ePACES), a web-based application
                          which will allow providers to create / submit claims and other transactions (e.g.,
                          Eligibility check and Prior Approval) in Health Insurance Portability and
                          Accountability Act (HIPAA) format. ePACES is a component of the eMedNY system,
                          which was developed on behalf of the New York State (NYS) Department of
                          Health. To contact eMedNY please email: eMedNYHIPAASupport@gdit.com or
                          call: 1-800-343-9000
 Health care provider     Entities providing health care to individuals, including Medicaid members. Health
                          care providers include providers of behavioral health, primary care, and other
                          licensed practitioners
 Homeless                 Homeless
                          As defined by U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) in 24
                          CFR 91.5, 4 categories of homelessness:
                              • Literally homeless
                              • Imminent risk of homelessness
                              • Homelessness under other federal regulations
                              • Fleeing / attempting to flee domestic violence

                          At-risk of homelessness
                          As defined by U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) in 24
                          CFR 91.5, 3 categories of at-risk of homelessness for:
                              • Individuals and families
[[p.15]]
 Term                     Definition and term details
                              •   Unaccompanied children and youth
                              •   Families with children and youth

                           (See Social Risk Factors, Clinical Criteria, or Covered HRSN Services for more
                          information)
 Health-Related Social    Any health-related social needs services that are NYHER-financed as approved by
 Need (HRSN) Services     the Federal Government

                          The scope of HRSN services is broader than NYHER-financed services that are
                          included as part of the SCN program. For simplicity, HRSN Services in this Manual
                          refers exclusively to services that are NYHER-financed as approved by the Federal
                          Government
 HL7 FHIR                 Fast Health Interoperability Resources (FHIR) is a standard for health care data
                          exchange, published by Health Level Seven International (HL7), a not-for-profit,
                          accredited standards development organization
 HRSN service provider    Entities contracted into the SCN that conduct NYHER activities and deliver HRSN
 (also “the Network” or   services (including but not limited to CBOs, health care providers, for-profit
 “organizations in the    organizations, etc.)
 Network”)
                          (See Roles and responsibilities of entities within the Social Care Network and
                          broader ecosystem for more information)
 ICD-10-CM                The International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification
                          (ICD-10-CM) is a standardized system used to code diseases and medical
                          conditions (morbidity) data. Health care providers use ICD-10-CM codes when
                          diagnosing patients. ICD-10-CM builds on ICD-10 (the International Classification
                          of Diseases, Tenth Revision)— the system used to code causes of death on death
                          certificates. Please see Social Care Coding document for SCN IT Platform
                          requirements
 LOINC                    Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) is clinical terminology
                          that provide a definitive data standard for identifying clinical information in
                          electronic systems. LOINC is one of a suite of designated standards for use in U.S.
                          Federal Government systems for the electronic exchange of clinical health
                          information. One of the main goals of LOINC is to facilitate the exchange and
                          pooling of results for clinical care, outcomes management, and research. Please
                          see Social Care Coding document for SCN IT Platform requirements

 Major life event         Permanent or fluctuating event in a member’s life that makes a member eligible
                          for reimbursed HRSN Re-screening
[[p.16]]
 Term                        Definition and term details

                             A major life event may be identified by any contracted entity within the SCN that
                             is authorized to have direct contact with a member (e.g., through Screening,
                             Eligibility Assessment, HRSN service delivery, service follow-up)

                             Major life events may include:
                                • Change in functioning (including an increase or decrease of symptoms or a
                                     new diagnosis);
                                • Inpatient or outpatient hospital admittance and/or discharge;
                                • Serious injury;
                                • Admittance, discharge, or transfer from detox or residential placement;
                                • Significant change in housing, including move to a different SCN region,
                                     move to different housing, or loss of housing;
                                • Significant change in income or support resources;
                                • Significant change to family, including but not limited to: marriage or
                                     divorce; giving birth (regardless of outcome) to or adopting a child, loss of
                                     a family member;
                                • Arrest;
                                • Loss of benefits;
                                • Change in coverage from FFS to Managed Care
 Medicaid billing social     OHIP designation for SCN Lead Entities
 care provider
                             Becoming designated as a Medicaid billing social care provider will enable SCN
                             Lead Entities to contract with MCOs to facilitate payment for the provision of
                             Screening, Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN Services for Medicaid Managed Care
                             members. Additionally, SCN Lead Entities will be able to bill via eMedNY directly
                             for HRSN Screening and Navigation of Medicaid Fee-For-Service (FFS) members

                             (See SCN Medicaid Billing Social Care Provider Designation and Enrollment for
                             more information)
 Medicaid Eligibility File   The Medicaid Eligibility File denotes Medicaid eligibility for FFS and Medicaid
 (MEF)                       Managed Care members as of the date it was pulled. The file is sent to SCNs via
                             the following pathway: OHIP/MDW to NYeC, then to QEs, and finally to the SCNs.
                             The Medicaid Eligibility File is sent on a weekly basis, and thus a member’s
                             enrollment may be outdated at point of contact with the SCN or their Network.
                             ePACES or MEVS Medicaid eligibility data is the most current source of Medicaid
                             eligibility status
 Medicaid Eligibility        MEVS is a component of the eMedNY system operated by New York State that
 Verification System         enables providers and other authorized entities to verify member eligibility and
 (MEVS)                      enrollment details in real-time prior to providing services and to obtain
                             authorization for specific services. MEVS is required to be integrated within the
[[p.17]]
 Term                      Definition and term details
                           SCN IT Platform as a permanent technical infrastructure of the SCN IT Platform for
                           the ability to query and verify a member’s Medicaid eligibility at the time of
                           service. To contact eMedNY please email: eMedNYHIPAASupport@gdit.com or
                           call: 1-800-343-9000
 Medicaid Fee-For-         Medicaid Fee-For-Service (FFS) is a payment model in which OHIP pays for services
 Service (FFS)             for Medicaid beneficiaries, directly paying participating physicians, clinics,
                           hospitals, and other providers a fee for each service they furnish. FFS members
                           whose HRSN Screens demonstrate unmet HRSNs and who are interested in
                           receiving support for those needs should receive an HRSN Eligibility Assessment.
                           For the SCN Program, the Medicaid FFS population will only be eligible for
                           Navigation to existing local, state, and federal services
 Medicaid Managed Care     Medicaid Managed Care is a health care delivery system organized to manage
 (MMC)                     cost, utilization, and quality inclusive of mainstream, HIV-SNPs, HARP, and MLTCP

sections.title: About this Operations Manual
sections.text:
2. ABOUT THIS OPERATIONS MANUAL
Purpose of this manual: The purpose of this manual is to provide program, billing, and data governance
guidance to SCN Lead Entities designated by OHIP.

This includes requirements governing the delivery of HRSNs services to New York’s Medicaid FFS and
Medicaid Managed Care members, as well as instructions related to data management, data security and
data sharing; and instructions for submitting reporting to support the integration of social, physical, and
behavioral health care within Medicaid.

This manual is a living document: This Operations Manual is a living document and will be updated frequently.
For questions regarding content in the SCN Operations Manual, reach out to: sdh@health.ny.gov

SCN Lead Entities may also direct questions to their OHIP contract manager.

Intended audiences: While SCN Lead Entities are the primary audience for this manual, it contains information
that is also relevant for several other audiences, including CBOs and other HRSN service providers, MCOs, and
health care providers (inclusive of behavioral health and primary care providers).
[[p.21]]
3. INTRODUCTION
Introduction sub-sections:
a. Vision and Goals for SCN Program

b. Overview of SCN Program Design

c. Overview of SCN Regions

d. Overview of HRSN Services

e. Overview of Entities in the Social Care Ecosystem

sections.title: Vision and Goals for SCN Program
sections.text:
a. VISION AND GOALS FOR SCN PROGRAM

i. Background
The mission of New York State is to protect and promote health for all, building on a foundation of health equity.
In New York and nationally, there is growing recognition that fully achieving health for all requires a focus not
only on physical and behavioral health, but also on HRSNs.
It is now widely acknowledged that addressing social needs such as food insecurity, housing instability, and lack
of transportation improves health and lowers health care costs. To ensure that these needs are consistently
addressed for New York’s Medicaid members, our state needs a coordinated infrastructure and set of processes
through which people’s unmet HRSNs can be identified, people can be connected to services to address those
needs, and the organizations who provide those services can be paid.

ii. What are Social Care Networks?
To meet that need, OHIP has established regional SCNs across the state to ensure that the HRSNs of Medicaid
members are more consistently identified and addressed.
Each SCN is comprised of a Lead Entity who contracts and coordinates with a network of CBOs and other
organizations providing HRSN services as well as other providers (inclusive of behavioral health and primary care
providers). Together, each Network will be responsible for ensuring that this is a seamless, consistent end-to-
end process in their region for HRSN Screening, Navigation, and delivery of HRSN services. This will require close
collaboration within each Network, as well as shared data and technology. All entities contracted into the SCN
for Screening, Navigation, and/or service delivery are collectively referred to as HRSN service providers
throughout this Manual.
Each region’s SCN Lead Entity will be responsible for driving this work in their region, including building,
supporting, and overseeing the Social Care Network.

iii. Goals for SCN program
OHIP’s vision is that the creation of SCNs will achieve four goals for Medicaid members:
[[p.22]]
•   Enable consistent, timely Screening using the NYS standardized version of the Accountable Health
    Communities (AHC) HRSN Screening Tool and Navigation to HRSN services
•   Create shared end-to-end visibility of the member journey from HRSN Screening and Navigation through
    delivery of HRSN services
•   Expand access to high-quality HRSN services
•   Strengthen collaboration between HRSN service providers and other partners in their regional health
    ecosystem, including, providers, care managers, and health plans

OHIP is committed to a SCN program that not only improves health outcomes for Medicaid members but also
does so in a way that advances health equity by helping to address long-standing health disparities and
supporting and strengthening existing work already being done by CBOs.

sections.title: Overview of SCN Program Design
sections.text:
b. OVERVIEW OF SCN PROGRAM DESIGN

i. Responsibilities of SCN Lead Entities
SCN Lead Entities are regional organizations charged with building strong Social Care Networks of contracted
organizations to collectively ensure consistent Screening, Navigation, and delivery of HRSN Services for the
Medicaid members in their area.

The core responsibilities of SCN Lead Entities include:

    •   Build and maintain a comprehensive Social Care Network of contracted organizations that collectively
        screen all Medicaid members in their region for HRSNs, navigate members with HRSNs to appropriate
        services, provide high-quality HRSN services, and provide data and reporting on these activities
    •   Enroll in the New York State Medicaid Program as a Medicaid billing social care provider. SCN Lead
        Entities will be Medicaid billing social care providers. They will be re-designated by NYS every five years
        and must also revalidate with the Medicaid program every five years. (See SCN Medicaid Billing Social
        Care Provider Designation and Enrollment for more information)
    •   Ensure more intensive coordination of HRSN services for Medicaid Managed Care members eligible for
        Enhanced HRSN Services. This includes individuals who are Medicaid High Utilizers, individuals enrolled
        in a NYS Health Home, pregnant and postpartum persons, criminal justice-involved populations with
        chronic or mental health conditions, high risk children under the age of 18, and people living with
        Intellectual and/or Developmental Disabilities, Serious Mental Illness, or Substance Use Disorders (For
        additional guidance on eligible members, see Medicaid Member Eligibility)
    •   Create a more accessible customer experience for Medicaid members seeking HRSN services through
        Social Care Navigation and Closed Loop Referrals
    •   Build the capacity of CBOs to provide high-quality HRSN services and to manage new or increased
        administrative responsibilities through capability-building and reliable funding streams
    •   Establish financially and operationally sustainable, self-innovating ecosystems that will continue to
        deliver services after the end of the NYHER 1115 Waiver amendment period
    •   Promote more equitable delivery of HRSN services and address the health, racial, ethnic, socioeconomic,
        and geographic disparities in existing access and quality
[[p.23]]
To achieve the above goals, OHIP will support SCN Lead Entities to become responsible for the coordination of
HRSN service delivery in each region (see Figure 3-1).

SCN Lead Entities will maintain and strengthen a comprehensive SCN of HRSN service providers responsible for
delivering evidence-based and member-centric HRSN services. This Network will also capture and share data
required for effective coordination between the SCN Lead Entities, HRSN service providers, OHIP, and other
stakeholders, to help evaluate the SCNs’ impact on health outcomes.

Figure 3-1: Overview of SCNs in context of broader health care and social care ecosystem

ii. Statewide SCN data and technology infrastructure
A critical component of the SCN infrastructure will be the creation of a statewide, multi-sector data and
technology infrastructure for HRSNs. This will require secure and actionable data exchange enabling delivery of
needed services to Medicaid members at the right place and right time, and data collection to enable the
evaluation of the SCN program’s impact on members’ health outcomes and health care costs.

iii. HRSN fee schedules

To ensure the financial sustainability of the delivery of these HRSN services, OHIP approved regional HRSN Fee
Schedules submitted by each SCN Lead Entity, with services approved by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid
Services (CMS), to reimburse HRSN service providers for HRSN services provided to eligible Medicaid members.
The HRSN fee schedule includes guidance on service delivery requirements for services to be reimbursed,
maximum allowable units, maximum duration, billing codes / modifiers, and rates / ranges / caps for each
service. (For additional information, see Payment Methodology for Services Delivered).

sections.title: Overview of HRSN Services
sections.text:
d. OVERVIEW OF HRSN SERVICES
OHIP has worked with CMS to establish criteria to determine which Medicaid members will be eligible to receive
specific, evidence-based HRSN services (e.g., Housing supports, Nutrition, Transportation, Care Management)
reimbursed using Medicaid dollars. These reimbursed HRSN services are referred to as Enhanced HRSN Services
(see Figure 3-2).

Medicaid members who have identified HRSNs but do not meet specific eligibility criteria will be navigated to
HRSN services delivered by existing state, federal, and local programs. Services provided by existing state,
federal and local programs for these members will not be eligible for Medicaid reimbursement as part of the
SCN program.
[[p.25]]
Figure 3-2: Social Care Network Enhanced HRSN Services

sections.title: Overview of Entities in the Social Care Ecosystem
sections.text:
e. OVERVIEW OF ENTITIES IN THE SOCIAL CARE ECOSYSTEM
SCN Lead Entities will work closely with their Networks to identify and address HRSNs among Medicaid members
in each region. They will also work with a broader set of partners (e.g., MCOs, providers, health systems, child
welfare service agencies, jails, local Departments of Social Services) to help address the needs of members.

i. Roles and responsibilities of entities within the SCN and broader ecosystem
    •   SCN Lead Entities: The OHIP-designated Lead Entity is responsible for:
            o   Network development: Organizing a Network of Screeners and HRSN service providers that will
                deliver HRSN Screening and HRSN services to eligible Medicaid Managed Care members. SCN
                Lead Entities will ensure the network has sufficient capacity to meet demand for Screening and
                HRSN services
            o   Screening and Navigation: Collaborating with partners in regional ecosystem (e.g., CBOs, MCOs,
                providers, etc.), screen members for HRSNs, validate member eligibility for Enhanced HRSN
                Services and navigate to the appropriate services, manage and close the loop on referrals, and
                deliver Enhanced HRSN Services through contracted HRSN service providers in the Network
            o   Network capacity building: Building ongoing capacity of Screeners, Social Care Navigators and
                HRSN service providers in the Network to meet demand for HRSN Screening and service
                delivery, via direct investments (e.g., support staff hiring, onboarding onto IT Platform,
                purchasing of necessary equipment such as computers), or through trainings and technical
                assistance
[[p.26]]
            o   Fiscal management: Contracting with MCOs to facilitate payments for HRSN services delivered
                by HRSN service providers, by becoming a designated Medicaid billing social care provider and
                submitting social care claims to MCOs
            o   Shared data and technology infrastructure: Establishing regional digital connectivity between
                the SCN, OHIP, and other stakeholders, and empowering organizations that work directly with
                members by providing necessary data through an accessible IT platform. This platform will
                support HRSN Screening and Navigation, data sharing and reporting, reimbursement of HRSN
                service providers, and claims submission. This role includes maintaining a clear set of business
                processes for data and technology activities and adopting interoperable standards for a social
                care data exchange, including integration with clinical data through the Statewide Health
                Information Network for New York (SHIN-NY)
            o   Data governance: Establishing data governance processes and procedures to manage both how
                data flows internally within the SCN and how data flows externally as it is exchanged between
                the SCN and other stakeholders outside the SCN, such as the MCO, OHIP, and external
                evaluators. Data governance includes ensuring that data is consistent, complete, interoperable,
                secure, discoverable, and trustworthy
            o   Performance management: Collaborating with HRSN service providers and MCOs on data-
                driven performance reporting to demonstrate value and continue to strengthen the evidence
                base on HRSN services’ impact in improving health outcomes, reducing health disparities, and
                reducing health care costs
            o   Operations and governance: Establishing and maintaining a governing body and executive
                leadership team that reflects and understands the unique needs of the region and effectively
                coordinates among other stakeholders in the region
   •   Community based organizations: CBOs are primarily responsible for delivering HRSN services. CBOs may
       also conduct HRSN Screening and Navigation to services for Medicaid members, if designated to do so
       by the SCN Lead Entity upon meeting specific criteria
   •   For-Profit Organizations: OHIP’s intent is that SCNs will be composed primarily of not-for-profit entities
       providing Enhanced HRSN Services. However, OHIP recognizes that there may occasionally be
       circumstances where inclusion of a for-profit entity may be necessary to ensure timely and consistent
       access to Enhanced HRSN Services. SCNs will need to communicate inclusion of for-profit entities in the
       SCN’s Network Composition Plan and Report. OHIP approval is not required for inclusion of for-profit
       entities in the Network. OHIP reserves the right to request additional information or clarification on
       inclusion of a for-profit entity and to request they be excluded from the Network in the event that non-
       profit alternatives are able to deliver Enhanced HRSN Services. If a for-profit entity is contracted into a
       SCN and delivers Enhanced HRSN Services but is later determined to be excluded from the SCN, they will
       still be reimbursed for services they have already delivered
       (See HRSN Network Capacity and Access)
   •   Medicaid Managed Care Organizations: MCOs are expected to contract with SCNs and will be
       responsible for the distribution of per-member-per-month (PMPM) payments to SCN Lead Entities.
       Funding will be provided to MCOs by OHIP for the purpose of making PMPM payments for Medicaid
       Managed Care members. MCOs will also be responsible for providing information to SCNs to help
       validate member eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services delivered by the SCN
[[p.27]]
       MCOs with access to the SCN Lead Entity’s IT Platform may also provide Screening and Navigation, if
       designated to do so by the SCN Lead Entity. MCOs are responsible for updating their educational
       materials (e.g., Member Handbook, Member Notice, MCO Presentation) to inform members about SCN
       services. Educational materials must be approved by OHIP prior to release
   •   Health systems and other health care providers: Health system partners and other health care providers,
       inclusive of hospitals and other physical health and behavioral health providers, will continue to deliver
       health care services to Medicaid members in their region. Health care providers that are already
       conducting HRSN Screening are encouraged to continue to do so. They may choose to become part of
       the SCN (allowing them to be reimbursed for Screening)
   •   Other Ecosystem Partners: Other ecosystem partners (including but not limited to local Departments of
       Social Services, jails, 29-I agencies, child welfare and preventative service providers, etc.), will be
       important partners to Networks. Ecosystem partners may refer members to the SCN for Screening
       and/or conduct Screening themselves

OHIP envisions these entities working together to ensure that the member experience from Screening to service
completion is seamless and that members can access services appropriate for their needs in a timely fashion.

services

sections.title: HRSN Network Capacity and Access
sections.text:
a. HRSN NETWORK CAPACITY AND ACCESS

i. Overview
The importance of strong HRSN Networks: For any service that Medicaid covers, OHIP knows that the service
cannot just be available in theory but should be easy, convenient, and equitable to access when and where
people need it.

For health care services, state Medicaid programs often require Medicaid Managed Care Organizations to meet
both network adequacy standards (e.g., requiring that all Medicaid members live within a defined distance in
miles or by minutes of car traveling time of a primary care provider in their health plan’s network) and network
capacity guidelines (e.g., requiring that certain functions are available during set hours and days, and that
routine activities are completed in a timely and culturally / linguistically appropriate way).

While some of the details of how network capacity and access are monitored are somewhat different for HRSN
services than for health care services, the vision is the same: consistent, convenient access to services that
meets people where they are in an equitable, customer-centered way.

Strong, accessible Networks are critical to ensure that SCNs effectively address members’ HRSNs and improve
their health outcomes. This includes ensuring that as much of the Medicaid population as possible is screened
for unmet HRSNs, that members with identified HRSNs are quickly and consistently connected to services, and
that those services are available in members’ communities from a diverse and culturally competent network of
HRSN service providers.

OHIP’s approach to HRSN Network capacity and access: To ensure strong HRSN Networks in the SCN program,
OHIP has established criteria for HRSN network capacity and access and will systemically monitor a set of HRSN
network capacity and access measurements to inform initial network composition and drive continuous network
improvement over time.

SCN Lead Entities are responsible for designing and maintaining a Network of organizations that can serve
members in each region. This entails screening all Medicaid members for HRSNs using the AHC HRSN Screening
Tool, validating member eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services, and referring those members to organizations in
the Network who will deliver the appropriate services.
[[p.29]]
Table 4-1 summarizes the network capacity and adequacy guidelines that SCN Lead Entities are held to by OHIP.
In some cases, these standards are requirements for SCN Lead Entities. In other cases, these standards are
guidance that is encouraged and will be monitored but are not required. SCN Lead Entities are accountable for
ensuring that these guidelines are met, which will require close collaboration between HRSN service providers
and other organizations in the Network.

OHIP understands that building HRSN Networks will be a new responsibility for many SCN Lead Entities, and that
achieving comprehensive and inclusive networks is an ongoing process. Inability to meet requirements will not
result in withholding of funds or resources while Networks are being established. OHIP plans to support SCNs to
achieve HRSN capacity and access through both capacity building funds and direct technical assistance.

HRSN capacity and access expectations may be revised over time as new program data is available.

Prioritizing diverse, inclusive, and culturally component networks: OHIP intends for SCNs to include
organizations who represent the diverse populations and communities that the SCN program will serve. This
includes the many HRSN service providers and other entities who already play a critical role in addressing the
HRSNs of Medicaid members today.

Towards that goal, SCNs should be composed primarily of non-profit organizations (per Federal Employer
Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS) of a variety of sizes and types, and in particular should include
organizations with annual budgets of less than $5 million. Each SCN should also be able to provide Screening,
Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN Service Delivery in the languages preferred by Medicaid populations in their
region. Social Care Networks should include not only a wide variety of HRSN service providers, but also all
interested health care providers, inclusive of behavioral health and primary care providers, and potentially other
entities such as local Departments of Social Services, local health departments, school districts, and others.

More information on the types of organizations, linguistic competencies, and inclusivity expectations for SCNs is
provided later in this section.

ii. HRSN capacity and access guidelines and requirements
SCNs are expected to achieve at least adequate HRSN network capacity and access across many functions. For

iii. Characteristics of SCNs
HRSN service providers will screen Medicaid members for HRSNs, navigate members to appropriate services,
and deliver HRSN services. Entities are required to be part of the Network if they wish to receive reimbursement
from the SCN Lead Entity for providing Screening, Navigation, and/or Enhanced HRSN Service Delivery.

OHIP intends for SCNs to include organizations representing the populations of the communities served. As
such, OHIP expects that SCN Lead Entities comprise their region’s Network with organizations and entities
according to the following guidelines:
[[p.32]]
    •   Organizational type (non-profit vs. for-profit): OHIP intends for Networks to be comprised primarily of

        non-profit entities. SCNs may include for-profit entities where necessary to support access provided that
        the SCN has already fully considered and included available non-profits capable of meeting OHIP
        requirements. SCNs are expected to communicate to OHIP the rationale for inclusion of a for-profit
        entity. OHIP does not need to approve each individual for-profit entity to be included in the SCN;
        however, OHIP reserves the right to request additional information or clarification on inclusion of a for-
        profit entity and to request they be excluded from the Network in the event that non-profit alternatives
        are able to deliver Enhanced HRSN Services. Preference should be given to non-profit organizations.
        SCNs should track and monitor that non-profits are receiving the majority of referrals (as their capacity
        allows)
    •   Organization size: OHIP intends for Networks to be comprised of organizations that vary in size. SCNs
        are encouraged to build Networks that reflect the diversity of entities in their region (e.g., including
        organizations with an annual budget of less than $5 million)
    •   Organizational competencies: OHIP expects SCNs to ensure all members in their region have access to
        Screening and Navigation in a timely manner using the member’s language of choice and individual
        accessibility considerations

iv. Language competencies for SCN organizations
Each SCN must have language competencies aligned with the languages that are common and preferred by
Medicaid populations of the region. This will be informed by a recent NY State of Health report on the preferred
written and spoken language of enrollees, as provided to SCNs by OHIP.

As of the June 9, 2024, NY State of Health report, the ten most common preferred written and spoken
languages, other than English, by the Medicaid population across New York are: Spanish, Mandarin Chinese,
Russian, Cantonese, French, Haitian Creole, Korean, Arabic, and Bengali.

SCNs may have individuals on staff with necessary linguistic competencies, or may contract with interpreter
services as needed, or both. SCNs are responsible for planning Screening capacity accordingly and reporting to
OHIP the specific language capabilities within the Network on an ongoing basis.

SCN Lead Entities should ensure the Network can be responsive to individual member needs, including people
with disabilities and with specific religious or cultural preferences. OHIP expects SCNs to operate in accordance
with National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Health and Health Care
(https://thinkculturalhealth.hhs.gov/clas).

v. Accessibility of Enhanced HRSN Services
OHIP expects SCN Lead Entities to establish a Network of HRSN service providers that is able to meet the unique
needs of members across an SCN region. While OHIP is not establishing HRSN service delivery requirements for
distance and accessibility, as additional data and information is collected through service provision, OHIP may
introduce additional specific requirements. Initial guidance includes:

    •   Distance to service provider: SCNs should ensure sufficient geographic coverage to minimize travel
        distance required for members to receive services
[[p.33]]
    •   Service accessibility: Enhanced HRSN Services should be provided in appropriate accessible formats (e.g.,
        virtual and in-person as appropriate)

vi. Ensuring broad and inclusive Social Care Networks
To best address the needs of underserved and hard-to-reach populations and ensure choice for members, OHIP
expects that SCNs will include a wide variety of organizations within each region that serve Medicaid members.

All interested and eligible organizations should be able to join the Network if there is a reasonable role they can
fill, including the HRSN service providers providing HRSN services as well as health care providers and other
organizations.

OHIP will establish a dispute process through which any interested organization with a reasonable role to serve
within the SCN can report their exclusion from the Network. Guidance on specific processes for disputes will be
defined in coming months.

    •   HRSN service providers: OHIP expects SCNs to include all HRSN service providers in the designated
        region that provide Enhanced HRSN Services and who want to join the Network. In addition, SCNs are
        expected to conduct outreach to HRSN service providers that are already grantees of New York State
        who are providing Enhanced HRSN Services to invite them to be part of the Network. OHIP will provide a
        list of relevant grantees to SCN Lead Entities
            o   These HRSN service providers may include voluntary foster care agencies (VFCAs), childcare
                resource and referral (CCR&R) agencies, and other grantees of the Division of Family Health, the
                Division of Chronic Disease Prevention, and the Division of Nutrition that are running programs
                providing HRSN services (e.g., WIC, Child and Adult Food Care Program, food banks, emergency
                food relief organizations, asthma prevention programs, nurse-family partnerships, family
                planning providers, early intervention, Children and Youth with Special Health Care Needs
                program)
    •   Health care providers: OHIP expects that SCNs will work with all interested health care providers that
        serve Medicaid members in each region as well as entities that coordinate care (e.g., Health Homes,
        Patient-Centered Medical Homes). SCNs should be inclusive of a variety of provider types, including
        major hospitals, primary care practices, health centers, behavioral health providers, and other entities
        providing care to the Medicaid population in each region
    •   Other entities: SCNs may engage with additional entities to ensure a robust Network, including but not
        limited to local Departments of Social Services, schools or school districts, Head Start programs, local
        departments of health and mental health, local housing authorities, HUD Continuum of Care (CoC)
        partners, and other government or non-government entities. Note that government entities may not be
        reimbursed for Screening, Navigation, or Enhanced HRSN Service delivery

In the event of consistent underperformance by HRSN service providers, health care providers, or other entities,
SCN Lead Entities may disenroll them from the Network.
[[p.34]]
vii. HRSN service provider & ecosystem partner complaints
In the event that a stakeholder interacting with the SCN Program has a complaint related to engaging with the
SCN program (e.g., exclusion from the SCN, issues with payments for Enhanced HRSN Services, etc.), OHIP
encourages the stakeholder to communicate their complaint with the relevant SCN Lead Entity.
However, at any time, stakeholders such as HRSN service providers or ecosystem partners may submit a
complaint directly to OHIP. In this case, OHIP will follow the process below:
Table 4-2: OHIP Complaint Review Process

 Step                   Details

 1: Stakeholder         •   Stakeholders may submit complaints via email to SDH@health.ny.gov
 submits complaint      •   Stakeholder complaints should include the following:
 to OHIP                     • Name of the organization submitting the complaint
                             • Name of the SCN Lead Entity involved in the complaint
                             • A narrative description of the complaint
                             • Timeframe of when the complaint occurred
 2: OHIP reviews        •   Upon receipt of the complaint, OHIP will:
 and resolves               • Review the complaint
 complaint                  • Engage the relevant SCN Lead Entity to resolve complaint
 3: OHIP shares path    •   OHIP may share a response to the stakeholder originally submitting the complaint
 to resolution with         that outlines an aligned resolution or path to resolution, as needed
 stakeholder

viii. Expectations for infrastructure funds and capacity building
Overview of infrastructure funding: OHIP expects SCNs to support capacity building for CBOs within the
Network. SCN Lead Entities will receive infrastructure funding to support development of the Network.
Infrastructure funds are used directly by the SCN Lead Entity and distributed to CBOs (CBO capacity building
funds).

Use of infrastructure funding for onboarding to the SCN IT Platform and technical assistance: SCNs should use
infrastructure funding to assist entities that are contracted with the SCN to provide access and onboarding to
the IT platform and training. In addition to funding, SCN Lead Entities are responsible for providing onboarding
support to contracted organizations in the Network for the following topics as needed:

    •   Setting up and using the SCN IT Platform
    •   Conducting HRSN Screenings using the AHC HRSN Screening Tool
    •   Completing Eligibility Assessments and Social Care Plan development
    •   Tracking referrals, service provision, and service completion
    •   Ongoing technical assistance

Capacity building funds for CBOs
[[p.35]]
Distribution and eligibility for CBO capacity building funds: CBO capacity building funds may only be distributed
by SCN Lead Entities to not-for-profit 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) charitable organizations that work at the local level
to meet community needs and provide HRSN waiver services to members. SCN Lead Entities will determine
distribution of capacity building funding across eligible CBOs that meet this definition. SCN Lead Entities should
ensure that CBO capacity building funding is distributed to build CBO capacity across a diverse set of CBOs in the
Network. Information on capacity funding and its uses should be shared with CBOs upon initial engagement or
shared alongside information about joining the Network. As a best practice, a method or process for obtaining
capacity dollars should be provided to eligible CBOs with or upon the execution of the SCN-HRSN provider
agreement.

OHIP strongly encourages SCN Lead Entities to create efficient, accessible processes to distribute capacity
building funding to CBOs (e.g., sharing clear information on requirements to obtain capacity building funding at
the start of the contracting process, using a simple application with clear criteria for receipt of funding).

Lead Entities may choose to make a portion of a CBO's capacity building funding award contingent on CBO
operations / performance to encourage CBO scale-up (e.g., contingent on the achievement of certain
milestones).

OHIP requirements for uses and tracking of funds (outlined in Table 7-1 Allowable uses of infrastructure funding
and eligible organizations) apply to all funds distributed to Lead Entities, regardless of whether funding is
contingent on performance.

Health systems or other health care providers as defined in this Manual, clinics, behavioral health clinics,
federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs), MCOs, local
departments of health, and for-profit entities are NOT eligible for CBO capacity building funds, but may be
eligible for capacity building funds for healthcare providers and behavioral health providers (see below for more
information). Health Homes run through FQHCs, behavioral health clinics, and health systems are eligible for
CBO capacity building funds, as long as the Health Home meets the criteria outlined below.

Health Homes and Care Coordination Organizations

Health Homes and Care Coordination Organizations (CCOs) may receive capacity building funds if the following
criteria are met:

    •   They have a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status and either of the following:
           a. They have a separate line of business that will provide HRSN Services which is operated in a
               separate division or unit from the portion of the business that is billing for Health Home
               Services; the line of business providing HRSN services must have separate books and records,
               staff, and management from the Health Homes business or are contracted with a SCN to receive
               referrals outside of the Health Home members from the SCN; or
           b. Health Homes and CCOs may receive capacity building funds to hire, onboard, provide
               equipment to, and train full or part-time staff (Social Care Navigators) if they provide Screening,
               Navigation and Enhanced Care Management to Health Home/CCO members and non-Health
               Home members that meet the enhanced (level 2) eligibility criteria

In general, Health Homes and CCOs may apply for capacity building funds on behalf of the separate line of
business providing HRSN Services. The line of business that receives and uses the funds must use the funds
[[p.36]]
towards delivering HRSN Services to members. This includes Health Homes run through FQHCs, behavioral
health clinics, and health systems as long as the Health Home meets the above criteria. Care management
agencies may receive capacity funding if they have a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status.

Allowable use of CBO capacity building funds: Allowable uses of funds for capacity building include direct
funding to non-profit organizations, such as:
    • Onboarding, training, and salaries for full- or part-time staff who provide services (e.g., conducting
        outreach to members, providing screenings & navigation)
    • Procuring equipment or technology required to launch or scale services
    • Investing in office space or operational needs tied directly to service delivery
    • Enabling program planning and development directly related to enhanced HRSN services

CBOs may receive both capacity building funds as well as payments for the delivery of HRSN services to
individual members.

OHIP encourages SCNs to use the following practices with regard to distribution of capacity building funding to
CBOs:
   • Providing upfront funds to cover time related to training, equipment, and start-up expenses
   • Allowing up to 12 months of salary and fringe for FTEs dedicated to the SCN HRSN Services as the
       volume of service payments ramps up
   • Assisting CBOs with calculating how the referral volume and rate will sustain staffing and overhead

10 business day. SCNs are expected to report components of their CBO capacity building in the Infrastructure
Cost Report (See SCN Reporting).

Capacity building funding for healthcare providers (HCPs) and behavioral health providers

SCNs may distribute infrastructure funds to healthcare providers—including hospitals, health systems, physician
offices, FQHCs, and behavioral health providers—to hire FTE Social Care Navigators. The purpose of this funding
is to increase the number of Medicaid members in different care settings with access to HRSN services.

Capacity building funds may be used for the salary and fringe benefits of an FTE Social Care Navigator who solely
works on the SCN program. These FTEs must be trained and onboarded onto the SCN IT Platform. SCNs will only
fund providers who serve high-needs populations in underserved communities (e.g., using hotspot data) and
whose patient population consists of at least 30% Medicaid members within their practice. Navigators must
conduct screenings, eligibility assessments, make referrals, and provide Enhanced Care Management to
members. Providers are also permitted to use their EHR to conduct the AHC screening and within the same day
have the navigator provide the members assessment and referral in the SCN IT Platform. The Navigators are
required to meet the SCN’s goals and metrics as criteria for receiving funding. Funding may also be used as
incentive or bonus payments for meeting metrics and goals set by the SCN.

Providers participating in the Medicaid Hospital Global Budget Initiative are not eligible to receive capacity
building funds. Documentation requirements for healthcare provider capacity building funds align with those of
CBO capacity building funds.
