iv. SCN referral tracking
Enhanced HRSN Service referrals will have a coding status that follows FHIR standards, allowing relevant
member referrals and data to be to be transmitted to and from the SHIN-NY Data Lake. HRSN service providers
will have process tasks within the SCN IT Platform associated with individual referrals that will automatically
transmit relevant data from the QE to the SCN IT Platform such that the HRSN service provider has all necessary
information to complete the process task. Conversely, HRSN service provider activity in process tasks (e.g.,
updating a referral’s status to be accepted) will automatically be timestamped and transmitted from the SCN IT
Platform to the SHIN-NY Data Lake.

The Social Care Plan and associated data elements that feed Performance Metrics will be created and
automatically tracked during the referral activity.

    •   Data Reference: Referral Activities
    •   Data Output: Social Care Plan Creation, SNOMED Referral / Service and Goal Codes (required year 3)

Technical considerations:

    •   Referrals will be assigned an appropriate standardized SNOMED-CT referral code provided by OHIP;
    •   Each referral is a “ServiceRequest” by FHIR standards
[[p.98]]
The SCN IT Platforms must be capable of the following functionality and details in order to conduct and manage
Closed Loop Referrals and service coordination between SCN Lead Entities and their Networks:

    •   Track where a member was referred
    •   Refer to Enhanced HRSN Services
    •   Referral Status (see Artifact 4 & 5 of 1115 SHIN-NY FHIR Implementation Guide for specific referral
        statuses)
    •   Time to Closed Loop Referral
    •   Details on services delivered (e.g., type of intervention, duration)
    •   Service Begin Date: SCN IT Platforms must allow for Social Care Navigators to utilize date of 1st service
        provision to calculate the service duration period when applicable (e.g., 6 months of MTM is based on
        date of 1st meal provision to the member)
    •   Service End Date: The end of HRSN service duration
    •   Total Service Units Allowed

OHIP plans to have all referral data:

    •   Flow from the SCN IT Platform through the SCN’s designated QE partner to the NYeC/SHIN-NY data lake
    •   Track important information about the Network’s referral closure rate
    •   Address any unmet Medicaid Managed Care member needs

The SCN Lead Entity will be responsible for reporting this information and additional performance detail
monthly to OHIP (discussed further in Performance and Payment section).

v. Distribution of Referrals across Network
SCNs should strive to ensure a balanced distribution of referrals across organizations in the Network.
Organizations providing both Navigation and HRSN service delivery are required to follow their SCN’s conflict of
interest plan to ensure they operate in the member’s best interests (see SCN Conflict of Interest Plan).

OHIP will not set distribution thresholds or requirements given the need to prioritize member needs and
preferences. However, SCNs should monitor and track distribution of referrals to understand from whom
members are receiving services and to inform how SCNs can continuously improve.
sections.change_note: L1 and L2 services should be marked "completed" by Navigators for SNOMED code accuracy; referrals issued as close to same day as the eligibility assessment as possible.

sections.title: Service Re-authorizations
sections.text:
f. SERVICE RE-AUTHORIZATIONS

i. Overview
As a guiding principle, Enhanced HRSN Services are not intended to be permanent solutions, and Social Care
Navigators should work to connect members to more permanent resources (existing federal, state, and local
services) where possible.

Six services can be re-authorized beyond the initial 6-month service authorization:
[[p.99]]
    •   2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation
    •   3.1 Nutrition Counseling and Education
    •   3.2 MTM and Clinically Appropriate Meals
    •   3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions
    •   3.4 Pantry Stocking
    •   4.1 Transportation

For Enhanced HRSN Services that can be re-authorized, if a member is interested in receiving continued services,
a new Eligibility Assessment will need to be conducted (confirming Medicaid eligibility, Enhanced Population,
Social Risk Factors, clinical criteria, and duplicative services) and is reimbursable. If a member is determined to
be ineligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, the member can only be re-assessed within a 12-month timeframe if
they experience a major life event, as defined in the Operations Manual "Glossary of Common Terms” (e.g., new
symptoms or diagnosis, housing change).

ii. Social Care Navigator workflow for service re-authorization
Social Care Navigators should follow the workflow below to determine if members are interested in continuing
service delivery and if so, whether they are eligible to receive additional services. Social Care Navigators should
still confirm Medicaid MMC enrollment (via MEVS or ePACES) on the day of the new referral (see Figure 5-5). If
the member is determined to be eligible to receive continued Enhanced HRSN Services for any of the above
services, then a new referral must be created.

Figure 5-5: Service re-authorization workflow

iii. Additional guidance for re-authorization of Nutrition services
When a Nutrition service requires RDN/CDN approval (as specified in section 5.j.vi), members will need a new
nutrition assessment with an RDN/CDN upon re-authorization. As part of the re-authorization for Nutrition
services, Social Care Navigators should ensure the following as part of the Eligibility Assessment:

    •   That the member is actively enrolled in MMC via ePACES/MEVS day of re-authorization
[[p.100]]
    •   That the member is still part of Enhanced Population

In addition, Social Care Navigators should ask the following questions and document responses in the Social Care
Plan:

    1. Can you prepare and serve adequate meals either by yourself or with the help of a caregiver?

        •   If member answers “No” - refer to MTM or Clinically appropriate meals (based on eligibility criteria)

        •   If member answers “Yes” - Continue to question 2 below

    2. Would you or a caregiver be able to prepare and serve adequate, nutritious meals if supplied
       with ingredients and instructions?

        •   If member answers “No” - Refer to MTM or Clinically appropriate meals (based on eligibility criteria)

        •   If member answers “Yes” - Refer to food prescription, food vouchers, or pantry stocking (based on
            eligibility criteria)

sections.title: Enhanced Services Member File
sections.text:
g. ENHANCED SERVICES MEMBER FILE

i. Enhanced Services Member File (ESMF) Overview
The ESMF will be a core data source used in determining members’ eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services. It is a
data file referenced during the Eligibility Assessment to identify members who reside within an SCN’s region and
details their eligibility information. The ESMF will:
    • Include all Medicaid Managed Care members
    • Identify members who reside in the SCN’s region (see Medicaid Member Eligibility)
    • Assist the SCN in determining member eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services by identifying eligibility
         criteria from MCO’s member records (e.g., Medicaid High Utilizer, individuals with chronic conditions)
    • See Information included in Enhanced Services Member File for the full set of information contained
         within the Enhanced Services Member File

ii. Process for creating, sharing, and auditing the ESMF
Process by which the ESMF will be created: OHIP will provide a state-prescribed ESMF Template to the MCOs.
MCOs will then use the ESMF Template to:

    •   Create their own algorithm to query all plan members and associated HRSN eligibility criteria
    •   Populate template with all plan members and their HRSN eligibility information
    •   Report all plan members, including members with voluntary or involuntary disenrollment

Timing for sharing the ESMF: Refer to the most recent version of the DSIG for time frame MCOs have to
transfer the ESMF file to the RRHIO. MCOs will work with the RRHIO to remediate data quality issues by the 4th
of the following month. On the 5th of each month, the QEs transfer regional ESMF to each SCN.

Process by which the ESMF will be shared: Once NYeC/SHIN-NY receives the ESMF from MCOs:

    •   SHIN-NY will send a monthly ESMF to New York State’s Medicaid Data Warehouse (MDW)
[[p.101]]
   •   The QE partner will obtain the ESMF from the NYeC/SHIN-NY’s data lake
   •   Each SCN’s designated QE partner will subsequently send to each SCN an SCN region-specific Enhanced
       Services Member File
   •   SCN Lead Entities and MCOs are encouraged to create any additional data sharing agreements they
       deem appropriate to facilitate this information-sharing

Figure 5-6: Process for sharing of ESMF

Process by which SCNs communicate to MCOs regarding new member information: During the Eligibility
Assessment, SCNs may learn new member information that may be relevant to MCOs per Table 5-16: Eligibility
determination pathways for each Enhanced Population and Enhanced HRSN Service. SCN Lead Entities and
MCOs will need to work together to establish a process by which SCN Lead Entities communicate this new
member information to MCOs.
OHIP will not require MCOs to update their ESMF data with information shared by the SCN Lead Entity.

iii. Information included in the ESMF
The ESMF must include all members enrolled in an MCO regardless of Enhanced Population status. See the latest
Enhanced Services Member File Template in the DSIG for the data elements and formatting requirements for
the ESMF.
sections.change_note: Navigators do not need further member support to verify a "yes" Enhanced Population or clinical criteria status noted in the ESMF.

sections.title: Changes in Member Medicaid Coverage and Relocation
sections.text:
h. CHANGES IN MEMBER MEDICAID COVERAGE AND RELOCATION
It is possible that members may experience changes in Medicaid coverage while receiving Enhanced HRSN
Services. OHIP aims to maximize member access to Enhanced HRSN Services while ensuring that members
receiving Enhanced HRSN Services are enrolled in a Medicaid Managed Care plan and meet eligibility criteria
requirements. The processes below are intended to support continuity of Enhanced HRSN services for members
covered by MMC plans in the event of a Medicaid coverage change.
[[p.102]]
For the purposes of this Manual, “members covered by a MMC plan” refers to all members who are actively
enrolled in Mainstream MMC, HIV Special Needs Plans (HIV-SNPS), Health and Recovery Plan (HARP), MLTCP, or
MAP.

i. Change in member MMC coverage
If a member experiences a change in Medicaid coverage while they are receiving Enhanced HRSN Services and
the member is no longer covered by a MMC plan, SCN Lead Entities should aim to ensure this information is
communicated to relevant stakeholders (e.g., member, Social Care Navigator, HRSN service provider) upon
notification of the SCN Lead Entity. SCN Lead Entities are responsible for ensuring that delivery of Enhanced
HRSN Services to a member end when the member is no longer covered by a MMC plan. OHIP encourages SCNs
to support individuals who are not covered by Medicaid to access existing federal, state, or local resources.

Guidance is outlined below regarding (1) members with upcoming potential changes in MMC coverage (e.g.,
disenrollment from MMC), and (2) members that have experienced a change in MMC coverage.

1. Guidance regarding members with upcoming potential changes in MMC (e.g., potential upcoming
   disenrollment from MMC): Member Medicaid coverage is typically re-verified annually. OHIP recognizes
   that some members will therefore have to re-verify MMC coverage while receiving Enhanced HRSN Services.
   SCN Lead Entities should ensure that Social Care Navigators will:

      •     Check MEVS for the latest information during the Eligibility Assessment: When creating a Social Care
            Plan, Social Care Navigators should consider the member’s upcoming renewal and prospective
            disenrollment date. For recurring services, the Social Care Navigator MAY (at the discretion of the
            SCN) refer the member for Enhanced HRSN service delivery only up until the renewal date /
            prospective disenrollment date, or the maximum service duration end date, whichever comes first
      •     Consider a member’s upcoming renewal date: When authorizing Enhanced HRSN services, Social Care
            Navigators should consider the member’s upcoming MMC renewal date / prospective disenrollment
            date. Social Care Navigators should make an effort to ensure services are delivered only to members
            that are enrolled in MMC with expected MMC enrollment through at least expected completion of
            Enhanced HRSN services (e.g., Home Modifications/Asthma Remediation)
      •     Direct members to existing re-enrollment programs and resources to enable MMC re-enrollment (e.g.,
            Certified Application Counselors, Marketplace Facilitated Enrollers and Social Care Navigators) if the
            individual has coverage through NY State of Health: Social Care Navigators and members can find the
            list of the over 5,550 statewide application assistors on the NY State of Health Website, which
            enables filtering of assistors by specific areas. For aged, blind and disabled individuals whose
            eligibility is determined by a local Department of Social Services, a Facilitated Enroller for the Aged,
            Blind and Disabled can assist in the application process
      •     Social Care Navigators are not required to directly support members with MMC or FFS re-enrollment
            (e.g., completing forms)

2. Guidance regarding members who have experienced a change in MMC coverage: OHIP expects that most
   members will be able to re-verify MMC plan coverage. In the case of a change in member eligibility (e.g.,
[[p.103]]
   member is disenrolled from a MMC plan), SCNs should establish processes consistent with the following
   OHIP guidance:
      • Verification of member eligibility in MEVS: SCNs are required to verify member coverage in MEVS.
         SCN IT Platforms are required to have integration with the Medicaid Eligibility Verification System
         (MEVS) in order to verify Medicaid eligibility using one of the MEVS methods. SCNs were provided a
         deadline of August 31, 2025, for MEVS to be embedded within the SCN IT Platform to enable a direct,
         real-time connection to eMedNY. SCN IT Platforms are only required to support the ability to query
         MEVS to verify a member’s Medicaid eligibility at the time of service using a HIPAA-compliant
         270/271 transaction.
      • SCN communication expectations: SCNs are expected to create a process to quickly inform their
          Network HRSN service providers of changes in coverage of a member receiving Enhanced HRSN
          Services
       •     Delivery of Enhanced HRSN Services: The SCN Lead Entity and HRSN service providers are responsible
             for stopping delivery of services to members who are no longer covered by a MMC plan and thus are
             no longer eligible to receive Enhanced HRSN Services
                 o  Home and Safety Modifications / Asthma Remediation: if a member disenrolls from MMC
                    while their Home Modification or Asthma Remediation is underway, SCNs must end
                    provision of the Home Modifications / Asthma Remediation and return the member’s home
                    to serviceable condition. Services should not be provided while the member is not enrolled
                    in MMC
            • Supporting previously enrolled members: OHIP acknowledges that members who experience a
              change in Medicaid coverage may need support in finding federal, state, or local resources,
              reenrolling in Medicaid, or communicating with their HRSN service providers:
                 o   If a member is disenrolled from MMC and subsequently enrolled in Medicaid FFS, Social
                     Care Navigators will be reimbursed for Navigation supporting members to find existing local,
                     state, and federal resources
                 o   If a member is disenrolled from Medicaid, a Social Care Navigator cannot be reimbursed
                     using waiver funds for providing Navigation services to the individual Social Care Navigators
                     may at their discretion connect individuals to other Navigation resources not supported by
                     waiver funds to access existing federal, state, and local services

ii. Member relocation and change of address
In instances in which a member moves across SCN regions during the course of Enhanced HRSN Service delivery,
OHIP aims for the member to experience minimal disruptions in service delivery while transitioning care to a
new SCN Lead Entity.

Updating member address: SCNs should proactively instruct members to notify their Social Care Navigator if
they are moving or plan to move. If a member’s address changes, the process for updating the member’s
address will proceed as follows:
    • Once aware of a member’s move, Social Care Navigators communicate address change with relevant
        MCO(s)
[[p.104]]
   •    Additionally, the member’s address needs to be updated by LDSS or NYSOH – at whichever entity the
        member is registered for Medicaid. Social Care Navigators should support MMC members in updating
        the member address with LDSS or NYSOH in a manner that best suits the member’s circumstances and
        needs and may bill time spent with the member to Enhanced Care Management
            o Social Care Navigators may work with members directly to help them contact LDSS or NYSOH to
                update their address; OR
            o Member can give live verbal consent to LDSS or NYSOH over the phone (e.g., three-way call) that
                a Social Care Navigator has authorization to speak on their behalf. Live verbal consent from the
                member is valid for 24 hours
            o Social Care Navigators may update member address themselves with LDSS or NYSOH as a
                member’s authorized representative (if a member is interested in receiving this support). To do
                so, members may submit an authorized representative designation form to LDSS or NYSOH to
                allow a Social Care Navigator to update an address on the member’s behalf. A Social Care
                Navigator may fill out the authorized representative designation form with input from the
                member, but must obtain a signature from the member before submitting the form to the
                relevant entity (LDSS or NYSOH)
            o If a member does not know whether they are registered with Medicaid at NYSOH or a LDSS, the
                member or Social Care Navigator may contact NYSOH at 1-855-355-5777 to determine where
                the member is registered
            o Additional guidance for NYSOH and LDSS is outlined below
   •    As part of the transition of care, the member’s Social Care Navigator in the original region should
        coordinate with the SCN Social Care Navigator in the member’s new region to ensure the member is
        appropriately re-screened and able to continue receiving needed services as quickly as possible

Table 5-10: Additional guidance for updating member’s address

                                 1-855-355-5777. Call center agents can speak with a Social Care Navigator
                                 directly, with either an authorized representative designation form
                                 completed or verbal consent directly from the member that the Social Care
                                 Navigator has authorization to speak on their behalf. The member will also
                                 need to provide their authentication information
                             •   Members can make updates in their online account at
                                 nystateofhealth.ny.gov. If members have an enrollment assistor, they can
                                 connect with the enrollment assistor directly in their online account to
                                 receive assistance

                                 DOB, SSN, CIN, new address, and AC# HX ID
 LDSS                        •   Members or an authorized representative can go in-person or call their LDSS
                             •   Eligibility workers at LDSS can speak with a Social Care Navigator directly,
                                 with either an authorized representative designation form completed or live
[[p.105]]
                                 verbal attestation directly from the member that the SCN has authorization
                                 to speak on their behalf
                             •   To update an address, the following data is needed: member first/last name,
                                 DOB, SSN, CIN, and new address

Member relocation scenarios
The following section provides guidance for Social Care Navigators on how to approach different scenarios
related to member relocation while receiving services.

Member moves permanently within same SCN region while receiving Enhanced HRSN services:
 o Member-specified residential address should be considered primary address for Enhanced HRSN Services,
    even if it does not match the address in MEVS / ePACES
 o Members may only receive services at one address that is considered their primary home address (with
    exceptions for minor residing in multiple households)
 o Social Care Navigators should document new address in Social Care Plan and initiate the process to update
    the member’s address (as outlined above)

Member moves permanently to a different SCN region while receiving Enhanced HRSN services:
 o Outgoing Social Care Navigator should initiate communication with the new SCN Lead Entity to discuss the
    member’s Social Care Plan and any urgent needs within 5 business days of becoming aware of the move
 o Outgoing Social Care Navigator should support the member to update their address via LDSS or NYSOH (as
    outlined above)
 o Outgoing Social Care Navigator may bill time spent on handover to Enhanced Care Management until
    member’s address is updated in MEVS / ePACES
 o All services from outgoing SCN should stop once the member’s address registered with Medicaid is
    updated
 o New SCN Lead Entity that is associated where the member lives will need to wait until member’s address
    is updated in MEVS / ePACES or ESMF to initiate referral to new service provider and restart Enhanced
    HRSN Services if needed

Member is temporarily relocating outside their SCN region:
 o Members will not be able to temporarily receive services in a different SCN region. Ongoing Enhanced
    HRSN Services should be temporarily paused while member is away
 o Social Care Navigators may refer members to existing federal, state, and local services that may be
    available during the temporary relocation

sections.title: Social Care Plans
sections.text:
i. SOCIAL CARE PLANS
[[p.106]]
i. Social Care Plan overview
Social Care Plans are individualized member records that help a Social Care Navigator identify a member’s
unmet HRSNs, develop goals and approaches to address unmet HRSNs, and track progress toward achieving
those goals. Per CMS requirements, each member in an Enhanced Services Population will have a Social Care
Plan developed by their Social Care Navigator while they are engaged with the SCN program. A member’s Social
Care Plan will be automatically initiated at the end of the Eligibility Assessment, and the same Social Care Plan
should be updated by the Social Care Navigator as needed throughout the duration of the time the member
engages the SCN program. The Social Care Plan includes details regarding member assessment and member’s
HRSNs in order to inform the services and care they receive. Each Social Care Plan will identify the member’s
unique needs, individualized strategies, and interventions for meeting those needs. Social Care Plans will be
completed in collaboration with the member and the member’s chosen support network as appropriate in a
culturally and linguistically competent way. Social Care Plans will be automatically generated within the SCN IT
Platform.

For members belonging to Enhanced Services Population(s), the automation for developing a member’s Social
Care Plan will be based on the member’s answers provided during HRSN Screening and during one-on-one
Eligibility Assessments with a Social Care Navigator. The Social Care Plan should be updated as needed by the
Social Care Navigator throughout service and with notes helpful to support service coordination by health and
social care professionals.

SCN Lead Entities are responsible for ensuring quality and comprehensiveness of Social Care Plans in their
Network. Specific processes for oversight and quality review of Social Care Plans may be determined by each
SCN Lead Entity. The Social Care Plan is a CMS and DOH requirement. Social Care Plans may be reviewed by
OHIP during the program to ensure consistency and comprehensiveness. SCNs do not need to regularly report
information on Social Care Plans to OHIP, but OHIP may request to review Social Care Plans at its discretion.
[[p.107]]
ii. Components of a Social Care Plan
The Social Care Plan is intended to be a living document that demonstrates an eligible member’s HRSNs and
detail on Enhanced HRSN Services. This form can continually be updated in instances of service renewals, major
life events, subsequent annual screens, or if any information is requested to be changed by the member or
anyone on their authorized care team. Any specifications for the unmet HRSN should be included in the Social
Care Plan as well as justification for the service.

Social Care Plans will only be viewable by the Lead Entity and organizations contracted into the SCN (e.g., HRSN
service providers) with approved user roles. HRSN service providers may only view a specific member’s Social
Care Plan if that HRSN service provider has received a referral to assist the member. HRSN service providers
viewing Social Care Plans must have necessary SCN IT Platform User Rights and permissions based on consent
received from the member, as determined by the SCN Lead Entity and their SCN IT Vendor, to view a specific
member’s Social Care Plan.

Social Care Navigators should document in the Social Care Plan all member information learned during
interactions with the member that is relevant to the SCN program and provision of Enhanced HRSN services,
including information obtained during the Eligibility Assessment.

In developing Social Care Plans, Social Care Navigators should ensure the following sections are included:

    •   General member information, including details on HRSNs that inform care goals and what services are
        most appropriate for the member
    •   Screening and Navigation history, including how the member was referred to the SCN and assessment
        notes from other care managers, if relevant
    •   HRSN service considerations, including the member’s Eligibility Assessment details that may inform care
        goals, service provision approach, individual goals, and service delivery information
    •   Close of service and member satisfaction, including details on service delivery outcomes and member
        experience

Person-Centered Goal Setting: Social Care Plans must include goals identified by the Social Care Navigator and
member to address member needs. SNOMED-CT codes for Person-Centered Goals Setting can be mapped to
goals in the Social Care Plan. Person-Centered Goal Setting codes are encouraged to be used in Year 1 but not
required until Year 3. For details on the relevant SNOMED-CT Codes, please reference the NYeC Extranet to view
the latest Excel.

Updating the Social Care Plan: Social Care Navigators should continually update the living Social Care Plan to
maintain up-to-date information on a member’s HRSNs and services and track progress toward goals. The Social
Care Plan should be updated at least annually and whenever a member:

    •   Undergoes an Eligibility Assessment
    •   Engages with the Social Care Navigator
    •   Experiences a major life event (e.g., significant change in housing, serious injury, inpatient hospital
        admittance)
        Has a change in their needs and/or services (e.g., member Social Care Plan goal is met, member receives
        services)

Coordinating with existing care plans: For all members in an Enhanced Population, SCNs are expected to ensure
Social Care Plans are distinct and separate from existing care plans covering clinical care, which is outside the
scope of SCNs. If the Social Care Navigator has access to an existing care plan for a member (e.g., a Health Home
care plan) that includes these details already, then these additional details do not need to be duplicated in the
Social Care Plan as long as this information is appropriately documented in the SCN IT Platform.

iii. Considerations for children and youth
As for all eligible members, SCNs are expected to develop comprehensive Social Care Plans for children to
inform the details of the Enhanced HRSN services required to best address each eligible member’s unmet
HRSNs.

Children with support of their parent, guardian, or legally authorized representative are encouraged to
contribute to discussions with their Social Care Navigator during development of their Social Care Plan.

Additional details to include in Social Care Plans for children and youth: Social Care Plans for children and
youth should include all the details described above, as well as:
    •   Household composition, including any other children in the household
    •   Identification of which household members are receiving Medicaid
    •   Identification of whether the child receives free or reduced priced school meals, if applicable, provided
        through the National School Lunch Program
    •   Name and relationship of individual completing the Screen on the member's behalf
    •   The school the child attends
    •   Whether they receive childcare outside of the home, and if so where
    •   Enrollment in Early Intervention services, school-based services, or other services for developmental,
        speech, or learning issues
[[p.113]]
    •   Enrollment in programs such as Health Homes Serving Children; and
    •   Services received within the Office for People with Developmental Disabilities programs or Office of
        Mental Health

iv. IT Platform functionality to enable Social Care Plans
Social Care Plans must be stored in the SCN IT Platform. The SCN IT Platform will be required to automatically
generate and save a member profile that includes the Social Care Plan for each member. The SCN IT Platform
must be able to:

    •   Store information about each member
    •   Allow for updates on an ongoing basis
    •   Store documents and notes collected by Social Care Navigators (e.g., provider attestation email, verbal
        consents, or forms for Eligibility Assessments, notes from ongoing meetings with members, member
        attestation documentation)
    •   Store documents and notes collected by HRSN service providers (e.g., notes from ongoing meetings with
        members, member documentation)

Social Care Plan data should be extractable from one location and automatically pull all needed fields into a
single, viewable document form which could be printed and made available upon request to a member or
anyone in a member’s authorized care team (e.g., a PDF report, single member page on IT Platform). Note that
Social Care Plans should be auditable.

sections.title: HRSN Services — Overview, Enhanced Populations & Social Risk Factors
sections.text:
j. HRSN SERVICES
[[p.114]]
i. Introduction to member eligibility and medical appropriateness
OHIP has defined evidence-based Enhanced HRSN Services that may be delivered by the SCN and reimbursed by
OHIP for the Enhanced Population. These Enhanced HRSN Services and associated eligibility criteria will be
posted on both the OHIP website and on the regional SCN websites. The following Enhanced HRSN Services will
be available in every region throughout NYS and will span the following social need domains: Care Management,
Housing, Nutrition, and Transportation.
A majority of the Enhanced HRSN Services may be reimbursed for up to six months. Medically tailored meals and
clinically appropriate meals are able to be reimbursed for an additional six months if the SCN determines that
the individual still meets the clinical and needs-based criteria. Select Nutrition services may be reimbursed for
up to 11 months for specific populations. Other services are limited as noted below.
Social Care Navigators may consider the member’s upcoming renewal / prospective disenrollment date in
making determinations related to Enhanced HRSN Service delivery. For recurring services (e.g., services that
require more than a one-time delivery), the Social Care Navigator MAY (at the discretion of the SCN) refer the
member for Enhanced HRSN service delivery only up until the renewal date / prospective disenrollment date,
whichever comes first.

In addition to helping to navigate Medicaid members to the most appropriate HRSN services, Social Care
Navigators will help ensure HRSN services are delivered in a manner that sufficiently address the needs of the
member. SCN Lead Entities will be accountable for ensuring that Networks have sufficient capacity to provide
Enhanced HRSN Services to address eligible member demand in the region.
OHIP intends for the SCNs to bridge members engaged with the following Enhanced HRSN Service domains
listed in this section (Care Management, Housing, Nutrition, Transportation) to existing local, state, or federal
services 60 days prior to the Enhanced HRSN Service duration ending, to the extent possible.
To be eligible for the Enhanced HRSN Services and to ensure the services are medically appropriate, OHIP will
require that an individual identified as needing Enhanced HRSN Services meet the following clinical and social risk
criteria as determined through the Eligibility Assessment:

service delivery is complete (e.g., at the end of 6 months), the member must meet the new eligibility criteria, as
determined in an additional Eligibility Assessment, in order to receive additional services.

sections.title: HRSN Services — Criteria for Documentation and Attestation
sections.text:
v. Criteria for documentation and attestation

A key required step of the Eligibility Assessment is the Social Care Navigator confirming the member’s eligibility
for Enhanced HRSN Services. Most criteria related to eligibility (both the Enhanced Population criteria and
clinical criteria associated with specific Enhanced HRSN Services) will be shared with SCNs through the Enhanced
Services Member File (ESMF) (see Eligibility Assessment Process and ESMF for more details). However, there may
be circumstances in which the Social Care Navigator must use additional information beyond the ESMF to
determine a member’s eligibility for Enhanced HRSN Services.

Circumstances in which a Social Care Navigator needs to use sources in addition to the ESMF:

    •      Criteria that are not included in the ESMF: There are a handful of criteria for which the ESMF will not
           provide information about the member (e.g., homelessness). For these criteria, the Social Care
           Navigator will need to ask the member to self-disclose this information in order to determine eligibility
           for Enhanced HRSN Services
    •      ESMF information is not fully up to date: Because the ESMF is based on historical claims data, there may
           be situations in which a member informs the Social Care Navigator of more up-to-date information than
           is included in the ESMF (for example if the member is pregnant, but that information is not yet reflected
           in the ESMF). The Social Care Navigator may learn this information during engagement with a member

OHIP has outlined different sources that may be used to validate each criterion (see details in Table 5-16). OHIP’s
goal is to maximize member access to Enhanced HRSN Services by creating multiple pathways for eligibility
validation while also ensuring services are provided to eligible members. The process for attestation is intended
to minimize burden on members, HCPs, and Social Care Navigators, while ensuring that member’s eligibility
determination for Enhanced HRSN Services is within the appropriate remit of each stakeholder (e.g., the Social
Care Navigator cannot make clinical decisions, care managers cannot make clinical diagnoses but can review the
member’s health records, etc.).

Who can attest:

    •      MCOs and Health Homes can provide a verbal attestation, a HIPAA compliant written email attestation,
           physical provider attestation form, or through care coordination notes in SCN IT Platform, if not
           otherwise directly supplied by the ESMF. As a best practice, SCNs should utilize the verbal attestation or
           email attestation process with the MCO or Health Home (when applicable) instead of through other
           methodologies
    •      Health care providers (HCPs) and other entity types listed below can either provide a HIPAA complaint
           written email attestation OR complete the physical provider attestation form. If a Social Care Navigator
[[p.130]]
        is unable to find a provider who meets the criteria below to attest on behalf of a member because a
        member has been treated by providers outside of NYS, SCN Lead Entities should reach out to their OHIP
        contract manager to discuss options
             o NYS licensed health care provider that accepts Medicaid members. NYS licensed health care
                providers are limited to: Physicians, Midwives (MW), Nurse Practitioners (NP), Nurses (LPN, RN),
                Doulas (Perinatal, Group), Physician Assistants, Clinical Psychologists, Licensed Clinical Social
                Workers (LCSW), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists, and Licensed Mental Health
                Counselors (LMHC)
             o Other health care providers that are part of programs within larger agencies that accept
                Medicaid members (e.g., Health Home, School-based Health Centers, Care Management
                agencies) and with access to necessary clinical information (e.g., member’s relevant medical
                records)
    •   Members can provide verbal attestation or written documentation for select Enhanced HRSN Services
        where permitted within Table 5-16

Member documentation is permitted for select Enhanced HRSN services per Table 5-16, the Social Care
Navigator should work with the member to develop a plan for how the member will obtain and submit required
documentation. The Social Care Navigator’s support and planning should include:
   • Sharing acceptable forms of documentation with the member.
   • Member name and DOB
   • Member Client Identification Number (optional)

Member attestation is permitted for select Enhanced HRSN services per table 5-16, Social Care Navigators will
ask members to provide verbal attestation to the criterion that must be documented by the Social Care
Navigator in the SCN IT Platform (e.g., via a checkmark confirmation in the SCN IT Platform). When completing
member attestation, Social Care Navigators may rely on the following script (outlined below) for criteria relevant
to the member and their potential unmet HRSN.

SCNs should integrate this member attestation confirmation capability into their IT Platforms. Social Care
Navigators are required to document a “Yes” answer to any of the questions below, if asked. Script for Social
Care Navigators: Tell member: Please answer the following questions with a "yes" or "no” answer:

    •   Pregnancy and Postpartum Status:
             o Ask member: Are you currently pregnant or up to 12 months postpartum?
    •   If pregnant or postpartum and interested in refrigeration units as part of medically necessary Home
        Modifications:
             o Ask member: Do you require refrigeration for storage of breast milk?
    •   Physical disability that limits independence: as part of the criterion for medically necessary Home
        Modifications (note: this service requires an attestation)
             o Ask member: Do you currently have a physical disability that limits independence in your home,
                such as difficulty walking or temporary paralysis?
    •   Heat or cold-related Illness: for the “at-home” criterion needed for medically necessary Home
        Modifications, including medically necessary air conditioners, heaters, humidifiers, dehumidifiers
             o Ask member: Have you experienced a heat-related illness (such as heat stroke, heat exhaustion,
                heat syncope, Rhabdomyolysis, heat cramps, or heat rash) that required an emergency room or
                urgent care visit within the last 12 months and occurred at home?
[[p.131]]
            o   Ask member: Have you experienced a cold-related illness (such as hypothermia, frostbite, trench
                foot, or chilblains) that required an emergency room or urgent care visit within the last 12
                months and occurred at home?

Social Care Navigator workflow to collect provider attestation:

The Social Care Navigator must ensure all forms of attestations are documented or uploaded into the member’s
Social Care Plan or Member’s Profile. Attestations are valid for 12 months from dated written attestation (i.e.,
physical form, email, care coordination notes, member documentation) or from date of received verbal
attestation. Sources for Social Care Navigators to validate member eligibility to receive Enhanced HRSN Services
outside of the ESMF include the options below. As best practice, Social Care Navigators should first rely on the
MCO’s or Health Home’s verbal or email attestation where indicated before utilizing a physical provider
attestation form.

    •   Verbal attestations are permitted ONLY from MCOs and Health Home providers. When a member is
        enrolled in a Health Home, Navigators should first reach out to the Health Home for assistance. All
        verbal attestations must meet the SCN LE's HIPAA requirements. MCOs and Health Home providers
        should review the criteria on the provider attestation form to verify the appropriate member diagnosis
        or condition for HRSN services. MCOs and Health Homes must include the below information in verbal
        attestations and Navigator’s should save the dated response within the IT Platform.
            o Member name and DOB
            o Member Client Identification Number (optional)
            o Entity name
            o MCO or Health Home name
            o Member eligibility criteria being attested to
            o Maternal or Child Health PHI disclosures (if applicable)
    •   HIPAA compliant email attestations are permitted from HCPs, MCOs, Health Homes and other entity
        types listed on the physical provider attestation form. Providers should review the criteria on the
        provider attestation form to verify the appropriate member diagnosis or condition for HRSN services.
        The email should include the below information:
            o Member name and DOB
            o Member Client Identification Number (optional)
            o Entity name
            o Facility name (i.e., MCO, Health Home, HCP business name)
            o Provider NPI
            o Medicaid Provider ID (MMIS) Number (if no NPI)
            o Member eligibility criteria being attested to
            o Maternal or Child Health PHI disclosures (if applicable)

A provider attestation form has been created by OHIP to streamline the attestation process for Providers, Social
Care Navigators, and members. The provider attestation form can be found on the following website:
https://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/redesign/sdh/scn/providers.htm.

If the Social Care Navigator determines that provider attestation is needed in order to support member
eligibility, the Social Care Navigator can request and receive provider attestation by either (1) the provider
[[p.132]]
submitting the OHIP standard attestation form directly to the Social Care Navigator through HIPAA compliant
transmission methods; OR (2) a member submitting the OHIP standard attestation form on behalf of their
provider to the Social Care Navigator. The provider attestation form can be simplified to clarify that a provider
only has to review and attest to select eligibility criteria that will support the member’s unmet need and
eligibility for select services.

The Social Care Navigator should work with the member to develop a plan for how the provider attestation
form will be completed and collected. The Social Care Navigator’s support and planning should include:

    •   Discussing with the member options for outreach to the provider with form and completion details
    •   Providing guidance for how the provider can submit the documentation to the Social Care Navigator
        through a HIPAA compliant transmission method
    •   Conducting outreach and follow-up, as needed to the member and/or provider to check on the status of
        the documentation. Social Care Navigators are encouraged to work with health care providers to
        communicate relevant member information (e.g., unmet HRSN) when requesting provider attestation

Provider attestation forms must be returned to SCN Lead Entities or any other HIPAA covered entities within
the SCN. The completed provider attestation form and the Provider’s individual National Provider Identifier
(NPI) must be stored on the SCN IT Platform. If the Individual NPI is not available, then the Medicaid Provider ID
(MMIS Number) may be collected

If the health care provider is attesting to any criteria included in the "Maternal or Child health" section of the
provider attestation form (e.g., pregnant or postpartum criteria) and sharing back with the SCN, the SCN must
provide to the health care provider a signed form regarding the disclosure of protected health information. The
SCN should sign and provide this form to the health care provider along with the attestation form. Per Table 5-
16 below, it is important to note that Social Care Navigators are allowed to accept a member’s verbal attestation
to their own status of being pregnant or post-partum without the need for requiring a provider attestation.

OHIP provider attestation guidance includes both forms:

   • Form for providers to attest to eligibility criteria
   • Form for SCNs to attest regarding the disclosure of Protected Health Information (PHI)
Provider guidance:

1. NYS licensed health care providers will need to attest that:
    • They are providing an attestation for enhanced populations or clinical criteria within their scope of
        authorized practice under state law; OR
    • They have sufficient access to information (e.g., electronic health record) pertaining to the clinical
        criteria/Enhanced Population.

2. Other health care providers that are part of programs within larger agencies that accept Medicaid members
will need to attest that:

    •   They have reviewed documentation from a licensed Medicaid-enrolled provider per eMedNY and can
        attest to the member meeting specified eligibility criteria.
[[p.133]]
If a health care provider at a rehabilitation center completes the provider attestation form or attestation email,
the rehabilitation center may need to coordinate with the member to obtain any necessary HIPAA release
permission / documentation to be able to share the form back with the SCN.

1. Care Management
Care Management involves Eligibility Assessment, planning, education, outreach, facilitation, member and non-
member facing care coordination efforts, and advocacy for options and services to meet an individual’s HRSNs
through communication and connection to available resources to promote member safety, quality of care, and
cost-effective outcomes. Social Care Navigators will work with members to connect them to the appropriate
services to address their HRSNs that align with the members’ preferences, limitations, disabilities, etc. Social
Care Navigators can perform Care Management for the Enhanced Population.
Care Management for either Navigation services or Enhanced HRSN Services will begin immediately by the Social
Care Navigator for any Medicaid member that has an unmet HRSN based on responses to the questions in the
AHC HRSN Screening Tool and has a completed Eligibility Assessment

sections.title: HRSN Services — 1.1 Navigation Services (Eligibility Assessment and Navigation)
sections.text:
1.1 Navigation Services (Eligibility Assessment and Navigation)
Navigation Services (Eligibility Assessment and Navigation) is only available for Medicaid FFS members and non-
eligible Medicaid Managed Care members who were screened, have an identified unmet HRSN and
subsequently receive an Eligibility Assessment under this service. These members may be navigated to existing
federal, state, and local benefits and programs. Medicaid FFS members and non-eligible Medicaid Managed Care
members will not receive access to Enhanced HRSN Services funded under the 1115 Waiver. Social Care
Navigators may bill for member and non-member facing time spent on the Eligibility Assessment and Navigation.
During the Eligibility Assessment and when navigating to existing services, Social Care Navigators will be
required to select granular ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT descriptions of a member’s unmet need within the SCN IT
Platform per the Social Care Coding document. After a member agrees to navigation, Social Care Navigators
must change the status to “Completed”.

1.2 Enhanced HRSN Services Care Management (Eligibility Assessment and Enhanced Care
Management for the Enhanced Population)
Enhanced HRSN Services Care Management (Eligibility Assessment and Enhanced Care Management) is only
available for eligible Medicaid Managed Care members that are part of the Enhanced Population eligible for
Enhanced HRSN Services.
1.2a Eligibility Assessment: Social Care Navigators may bill for member and non-member facing time spent on
the Eligibility Assessment for the Enhanced Population per the HRSN Fee Schedule, “Enhanced HRSN Care
Management – Eligibility Assessment Level 2 Only”. During the Eligibility Assessment and when making referrals,
Social Care Navigators will be required to select granular ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT description of a member’s
unmet need. Following the Eligibility Assessment, Social Care Navigators will also be required to select granular
ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT to capture the specific nature of Navigation support provided and specific Enhanced
HRSN services to which members are referred.
1.2b Enhanced Care Management: For the NYHER population eligible for Enhanced HRSN Services, the Social
Care Navigator has the responsibility of providing Enhanced Care Management which includes: referral
management, member facing and non-member facing care coordination (including connection to clinical care
management), education and confirming with the member whether the referral was accessed and whether their
needs were met. Social Care Navigators will coordinate, if applicable, the application process and application
fees to assist members in securing essential services such as housing, transportation, employment, etc.
Examples of covered costs include costs associated with obtaining copies of vital records (i.e. birth certificate),
obtaining non-driver identification, driver’s license application fees at the DMV, background check fees, and
housing application fees.
 Social Care Navigators may bill for member and non-member facing time spent on Enhanced Care Management
per the HRSN Fee Schedule under procedure codes for Enhanced HRSN Care Management – Care Management
Level 2 Only and Enhanced Care Management – Follow Up Level 2 Only.
The Social Care Navigator may use Enhanced Care Management codes to bill for member and non-member
facing time spent making and managing member referrals and conducting follow-ups before and after service
delivery (per Table 5-9) for all Enhanced HRSN Services. Social Care Navigators may also use Enhanced Care
[[p.158]]
Management codes to bill for navigating members transitioning from Enhanced HRSN Services to existing
federal, state, and local resources.
The Social Care Navigator may also use Enhanced Care Management procedure codes to bill for member and
non-member facing time spent on coordination activities related to select Enhanced HRSN services (outlined
below) for the member if the contracted HRSN service provider is not performing coordination for the services.
If the HRSN service provider does conduct the coordination, they should bill according to guidance for each
service (see individual services in Covered HRSN Services).
    •    Transportation (e.g., arrange private transportation, coordinate public transportation vouchers)
    •    Cooking Supplies (e.g., discuss cooking supplies needs with member, order cooking supplies)
    •    Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications (e.g., submit SOW for Technical Review, review SOW and
         select services, get member approval for services)
    •    Home Remediation Service (e.g., submit SOW for Technical Review, review SOW and select services, get
         member approval for services)
    •    Asthma Remediation (e.g., call member to determine timing for ASME visit, review findings from ASME
         visit, submit SOW for Technical Review, review SOW and select services)
    •    Community Transitional Supports (CTS) (e.g., discuss furnishing needs, collecting bills or receipts)
    •    Utility Setup / Assistance (e.g., collect utility bills from member, coordinate utility bill payments)
    •    Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back Rent) (e.g., submit rental payments directly to
         landlord)
    •    Recuperative Care (Medical Respite) (e.g., coordinate transitional services with MRP prior to member
         discharge)

The Social Care Navigator will further create Social Care Plans with the member to determine ongoing needed
services including Enhanced HRSN Services, refer, track, and follow-up with services the member is eligible for
and opts into.

SCN LEs must establish a workflow to ensure members are connected via a warm hand-off to clinical care
management providers when members are interested and potentially eligible for services; connection to clinical
care management is billable under Enhanced Care Management.

2. Housing
The New York’s 1115 Waiver makes available several Housing support services to meet enrolled Medicaid
Managed Care member’s needs. These Housing supports are intended to create housing equity, accessibility,
safety, and sustainability to help prevent adverse health and social impacts.
When HRSNs are not directly addressed by the below Housing / Utility services (e.g., fire alarms, lead paint
exposure programs, etc.), the Social Care Navigator may refer members to existing federal, state, and local
services. SCNs can accept a member’s verbal attestation of services received to-date from their MLTCP/MAP
plan pertaining to the below services:
    •   2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications
    •   2.2 Home Remediation
    •   2.3 Asthma Remediation
    •   2.8 CTS
    •   2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services
Social Care Navigators may refer MLTCP and MAP members to other housing services without coordinating with
a member’s MCO case manager but are encouraged to do so to support member experience and coordination.
i. Non-Invasive Measures and Asthma Trigger Remediation Services/Asthma Supportive Products
Under services 2.1 Home Modification, 2.2 Home Remediation, and 2.3 Asthma Remediation, specific services
that are not considered an invasive measure do not need SOW TA approval. An Invasive Measure is defined as
any residential modification or remediation that may have a detrimental health, safety, or building impact on
the member(s) or household if not properly installed and inspected. Such invasive measures require landlord
approval.
[[p.160]]
For dwellings requiring deep cleaning prior to proceeding with the provision of home modifications, mold
remediation and/or Integrated Pest Management (IPM), cleaning services can be billed towards the member’s
overall cap within 2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications, 2.2a Mold and Pest Remediation, 2.2b
Ventilation Improving Systems or 2.3 Asthma Remediation and provided prior to SOW development or SOW
technical review if needed.
If the member or landlord does not consent to invasive measures within the SOW, the Social Care Navigator can
still offer the member the below non-invasive measures without a SOW. The Social Care Navigator must track
the costs of these non-invasive measures towards the member’s overall cap in addition to any subsequent costs
defined in the SOW.
2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications:
            2.1a Non-skid surfaces
2.2 Home Remediation Service:

            2.2b Ventilation Improving Systems: Medically necessary improvement of ventilation systems, which
            include provisions of devices and appliances that are eligible by clinical criteria:
                 o   Air conditioners;
                 o   Heaters (i.e., electric space heaters with automatic shut-off safety feature)
                 o   Humidifiers;
                 o   Dehumidifiers;
                 o   Air filtration devices (which may be limited to mechanical only)
        2.2c Equipment Provision: Provision of medically necessary mini refrigeration units as needed for
        medical treatment and prevention (e.g., insulin)
2.3 Asthma Remediation: Trigger Remediation Services and Asthma Supportive Products
The following asthma trigger remediation services and asthma supportive products are considered non-invasive
and may be provided by the ASME provider AND given to the member prior to SOW development if needed.
If the member declines proceeding with 2.3b (the dwelling assessment and SOW development) or if the landlord
does not consent to a SOW including invasive measures, the Social Care Navigator should proceed with the full
scope of 2.3a (ASME) which includes initial ASME visit, final ASME visit, and provision of non-invasive supportive
products if necessary under 2.2a Mold and Pest Remediation, 2.2b Ventilation Improving Systems and 2.3
Asthma Remediation, and Enhanced Care Management. The Social Care Navigator must track the costs of non-
invasive measures towards the member’s overall cap within 2.2a Mold and Pest Remediation, 2.2b Ventilation

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications
sections.text:
2.1 Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications
These services are available for a home that is owned, rented, leased, or occupied by the Medicaid member or
their caregiver. Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications consist of the following elements:
   •   Dwelling Assessment & SOW Development: A comprehensive dwelling assessment of the primary
       residence to identify Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications needed. Assessment should be
       conducted by a qualified home improvement contractor with industry-standard credentials in building
       science. The SOW should outline recommended Home Modifications based on the assessment. Both the
       HRSN service provider and contractors’ coordination and administrative costs should be included in the
       SOW and should not exceed 10% of the total costs of the project

   •   SOW Technical Review: Each SOW should be reviewed by a qualified reviewer with industry-standard
       credentials in building science, working independently of the HRSN service provider that performs the
       Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications installation. The SOW Technical Review should indicate
       which services in the SOW are invasive. If the SOW includes invasive measures, written approval from
       the property owner (landlord in case of a rental) is required before beginning work (approval must be
       obtained by either the Social Care Navigator or service provider)

   •   Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications: Limited internal or external physical adaptations made to
       eligible member’s home or community dwelling when necessary to ensure maximum health, welfare,
       and safety, or to allow the member to live independently in a community-based setting. All installation
       services include general education on how to use and properly care for equipment during installation.

            Medically necessary Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications that are eligible by clinical criteria:
               o Accessibility ramps
               o Handrails; Grab bars
               o Electric door openers,
               o Widening of doorways; Pathways
               o Door and cabinet handles
               o Bathroom facilities; Kitchen cabinet or sinks; Non-skid surfaces
               o Home Modifications will be limited to those listed above and which are recommended in
                   the SOW and approved by the Social Care Navigator after the SOW Technical Review.

            Member written approval is required to begin installation of approved SOW services. Services
            involving invasive measures require written approval from the property owner (landlord, if the
            residence is rented). HRSN service providers must provide proof of credentials/licensure/industry-
            accepted certifications and training (including advanced requirements for specialized services such
            as HVAC, IPM, etc.). Total costs of services for Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications and
            Home Remediation may not exceed per member cap listed in the HRSN Fee Schedule for duration of
            Waiver period

   •   Quality Assurance (QA) Inspection: Within 90 days of service completion, a QA Inspection should be
       conducted in alignment with Building Performance Institute (BPI) and other industry technical standards
       for QA for a minimum of 10 percent of households where Home Accessibility and Safety Modification
       services are provided by the SCN. QA provider should be independent of provider of Home Accessibility
[[p.163]]
         and Safety Modifications. If a QA Inspection identifies any issues with the work completed, the Social
         Care Navigator should work with the HRSN service provider to ensure work passes the QA Inspection.

                         credentials/ licensure and/or industry-accepted certifications and training specific to
                         the services being proposed. Physical adaptations to a residence must be performed
                         by an individual holding a New York State Contractor’s License
                         4. Either the SCN or a contracted organization that is part of the Network can contract
                         with the modification / remediation / ventilation company
                         5. Modifications must be conducted in accordance with applicable state and local
                         building codes
                         6. Dwelling Assessment and SOW Development must be conducted by a qualified
                         home improvement contractor with proof of industry-standard credentials in building
                         science
                         7. SOW Technical Review and QA Inspection must be conducted by a qualified
                         reviewer/inspector holding industry-standard credentials in building science and
                         working independently of the HRSN service provider for Home Accessibility and
                         Safety Modifications
                         8. HRSN service providers completing Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications
                         must have proof of credentials/licensure/industry-accepted certifications and
                         trainings AND demonstrated experience providing Home Modifications

Workflow for Home Accessibility / Safety Modification Service: The SCN Lead Entity will need to create a
unique workflow for Home Accessibility / Safety Modification services based on the Dwelling Assessment, SOW
Development, Home Modifications, and QA Inspection. In general, the workflow should follow the below steps
(see Figure 5-7 for a visual process flow):
   1. The Social Care Navigator will refer the member to an HRSN service provider to complete a Dwelling
      Assessment and develop an SOW.
   2. The HRSN service provider will conduct the Dwelling Assessment and SOW Development and provide
      the SOW to the Social Care Navigator via the IT Platform. The SOW will include the physical adaptations
      and modifications necessary to ensure maximum health, welfare, and safety, or to allow the member to
      function independently in their home. Only one Dwelling Assessment and SOW is required. The provider
      that conducts the Dwelling Assessment and develops the SOW can be reimbursed for admin time,
      including travel.
[[p.165]]
    3. The Social Care Navigator will submit the SOW for Technical Review to a qualified reviewer holding
        industry-standard credentials in building science working independently of the HRSN service provider for
        the Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications.
    4. The provider conducts the SOW Technical Review, indicates within the SOW which services involve
        invasive measures, and returns the SOW to the Social Care Navigator.
    5. The Social Care Navigator will review the SOW and select the appropriate services to authorize for the
        member to receive (Note: HRSN service provider may recommend services that are not covered under
        the NYHER Enhanced HRSN Services. In those instances, the Social Care Navigator may connect member
        to applicable federal, state, local programs). The total cost for Home Accessibility and Safety
        Modification services must be at or below the allowable cap amount in the HRSN Fee Schedule. If
        recommended services are above the allowable cap, the Social Care Navigator, in consultation with the
        Technical Reviewer, must prioritize appropriate services to authorize for the member to remain under
        the cap. The Social Care Navigator must enter and create unique referrals for each service included in
        the approved SOW and document authorized services within the Social Care Plan.
    6. The Social Care Navigator must ensure member written approval of approved SOW services to begin
        modification services. Any SOW involving invasive measures, as confirmed by the SOW Technical
        Review, also requires written approval from the property owner (landlord, if the residence is rented).
    7. The Social Care Navigator makes a referral to HRSN service provider for Home Accessibility and Safety
        Modifications. Service providers for Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications and/or their
        subcontractors must provide proof of credentials/licensure/industry-accepted certifications and
        training. The HRSN service provider or subcontractor proceeds with completing Home Accessibility and
        Safety Modifications as approved in the SOW. The HRSN service provider for Home Accessibility and
        Safety Modifications may be the same or different entity for the Dwelling Assessment and SOW
        Development.
    8. Provider completes Home Accessibility and Safety Modification services.
    9. For a minimum of 10 percent of households where Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications services
        are provided (as determined at the discretion of the SCN Lead Entity), QA Inspection should be
        conducted by a qualified inspector holding industry-standard credentials in building science, within 90
        days of completion of Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications. Provider of QA Inspection must be
        independent of the HRSN service provider for Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications. If a QA
        Inspection identifies any issues with the work completed, the Social Care Navigator should work with
        the HRSN service provider to ensure work passes the QA Inspection.
    10. The HRSN service provider for Home Accessibility and Safety Modifications updates the SCN IT Platform
        to demonstrate the services within the SOW have been completed.
    11. The Social Care Navigator documents the completed services within the Social Care Plan and follows up
        with the member within 5 business days to document their satisfaction.

Note: If the cost of services is $2,000 or more, the HRSN service provider must either:
   a. Obtain at least three bids for any total work of $2,000 or more and select the lowest price and best
         value or substantially equivalent bid, if applicable. As a last resort, the SCN Lead Entity may move
         forward with only two bids if there is limited capacity within SCN region.
   b. If preferred, the SCN Lead Entity can establish a list of preferred contractors through a competitive
         bidding process to be updated annually, and the HRSN service provider can select a contractor for
         recommended modifications from this list without soliciting at least 3 bids for each service.
[[p.166]]
Across both options, bid development (e.g., time spent traveling to the site, writing up the bid) will not be
reimbursed.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.2 Home Remediation Services
sections.text:
2.2 Home Remediation Services
These services are available for a home that is owned, rented, leased, or occupied by the Medicaid member or
their caregiver. Home Remediation Service will consist of the following elements:
    •   Dwelling Assessment & SOW Development: A comprehensive dwelling assessment of the primary
        residence to identify Home Remediation Service needed. Assessment should be conducted by a
        qualified home improvement contractor with industry-standard credentials in building science. The SOW
        should outline recommended Home Modifications based on the assessment. Both the HRSN service
        provider and contractors’ coordination and administrative costs should be included in the SOW and
        should not exceed 10% of the total costs of the project
    •   SOW Technical Review: Each SOW should be reviewed by a qualified reviewer with industry-standard
        credentials in building science, working independently of the HRSN service provider that performs the
        Home Remediation Service. The SOW Technical Review should indicate which services in the SOW are
        invasive. If the SOW includes invasive measures, written approval from the property owner (landlord in
        case of a rental) is required before beginning work (approval must be obtained by either the Social Care
        Navigator or service provider)
    •   Home Remediation Services: Home Remediation Services are limited to repairs or remediations to an
        eligible member’s home or community dwelling. They are a cost-effective method for addressing the
[[p.167]]
         occupant’s health condition and must be recommended by a health care professional or indicated on
         the MCO’s Enhanced Services Member File. Total combined costs of services for Home Accessibility and
         Safety Modifications and Home Remediations may not exceed per member cap listed in HRSN Fee
         Schedule for duration of Waiver period
         These services and provisions in 2.2a, 2.2b and 2.2c are available in a home that is owned, rented,
         leased, or occupied by the eligible Medicaid member or their caregiver. Member written approval is
         required to begin installation of approved SOW services. Services involving invasive measures require
         written approval from the property owner (landlord, if the residence is rented). HRSN service providers
         must provide proof of credentials/licensure/industry-accepted certifications and training (including
         advanced requirements for specialized services such as HVAC, IPM, etc.)
    •    QA Inspection: Within 90 days of service completion, a QA Inspection should be conducted in alignment
         with Building Performance Institute (BPI) and other industry technical standards for QA for a minimum
         of 10 percent of households where Home Remediation Services is provided by the SCN. QA provider
         should be independent of provider of Home Remediation Services. If a QA Inspection identifies any
         issues with the work completed, the Social Care Navigator should work with the HRSN service provider
         to ensure work passes the QA Inspection
2.2a Mold and Pest Remediation: Home Remediation Services to promote member’s health and wellbeing
may include:

    •    Mold remediation (including fixing water leaks and removing damp or wet items to prevent mold
         growth).
    •    Pest remediation (including sealing / patching holes and cracks through which pests can enter the
         home).

2.2b Ventilation Improving Systems: Medically necessary improvement of ventilation systems, which include
provisions of devices and appliances that are eligible by clinical criteria:

    •    Air conditioners;
    •    Humidifiers;
    •    Dehumidifiers;
    •    Heaters (i.e., electric space heaters with automatic shut-off safety feature);
    •    Air filtration devices (which may be limited to mechanical only).

2.2c Equipment Provision: Provision of medically necessary mini refrigeration units as needed for medical
treatment and prevention (e.g., insulin)

      The provider that conducts the Dwelling Assessment and develops the SOW can be reimbursed for

   3. The Social Care Navigator will submit the SOW for Technical Review to a qualified reviewer holding

      Home Remediation Service.
   4. The provider conducts the SOW Technical Review and indicates within the SOW which services involve
      invasive measures and returns the SOW to the Social Care Navigator.
   5. The Social Care Navigator will review the SOW and select the appropriate services to authorize for the

[[p.170]]
        appropriate services to authorize for the member to remain under the cap. The Social Care Navigator

    6. The Social Care Navigator must ensure member written approval of approved SOW services to begin
        remediation services. Any SOW involving invasive measures, as confirmed by the SOW Technical review,

    7. The Social Care Navigator makes referral to HRSN service provider for Home Remediation Service.
        Service providers and/or their subcontractors must provide proof of credentials/licensure/industry-

    8. HRSN service provider completes Home Remediation Service.
