sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.3 Asthma Remediation
sections.text:
2.3 Asthma Remediation
Remediation services will be available to Enhanced Population members who have a diagnosis of asthma and
meet the clinical criteria in Table 5-15. SCN LEs are encouraged to coordinate with their SCN IT Platform vendor
to obtain an aggregate ESMF file across MCOs. The aggregate ESMF list can then be filtered by the indicator for
Uncontrolled Asthma and shared with contracted partners for targeted outreach attempts.
These services are available for a home that is owned, rented, leased, or occupied by the Medicaid member or
their caregiver. Asthma Remediation services entail the provision of remedial services to remove indoor
environmental allergens and the provision of supportive products to eliminate or reduce asthma triggers in the
[[p.171]]
member’s home. Remediation services will be tailored to the individual needs of the member and the primary
residence (owner-occupied or rental dwelling) of the member. Services should address multiple triggers to
improve the residence and member’s capacity for asthma self-management. Asthma Remediation services will
include the following components:
2.3a Asthma Self-Management Education (ASME): Health education tailored to the needs of the member and
family/caregivers to expand asthma knowledge, such as early warning signs and management of worsening
symptoms, asthma control and medication adherence, and identification and reduction of asthma triggers.
ASME should be conducted in alignment with NIH national asthma guidelines and support education for a
partnership in asthma care. ASME must be provided by a qualified nonphysician health care professional, such
as a certified asthma educator specialist (AE-C), respiratory therapist (RT), or specially trained lay health worker
(e.g., health educator, community health worker (CHW), etc.), with documented training and demonstrated
competency in delivering guidelines-based Asthma Self-Management Education and comprehensive home
environmental assessments to identify and provide education on reducing asthma triggers. ASME must include
an asthma and environmental assessment performed in two separate visits. The ASME provider must notify the
Social Care Navigator if the member has additional care coordination needs outside of the ASME service (e.g.,
clinical follow-up) unless the ASME provider is also contracted as a Social Care Navigator. The ASME provider can
supply asthma supportive products and indoor allergen reduction products and bill them towards the member’s
cap.
        NOTE: If the member declines proceeding with 2.3b (the dwelling assessment and SOW development) or
        if the landlord does not consent to a SOW including invasive measures, the Social Care Navigator should
        proceed with the full scope of 2.3a (ASME) which includes initial ASME visit, final ASME visit, Enhanced
        Care Management, provision of non-invasive products and services per Section 2.i Non-Invasive
        Measures and Asthma Trigger Remediation Services/Asthma Supportive Products, and provision of
        additional education to the member between visits if needed (billable to 24 units cap for ASME Home
        Visits).
Specifications for each visit are as follows:

    •   Initial Visit: must be conducted in-person or via video call in the member’s dwelling to provide initial
        asthma and home environmental assessments and ensure appropriateness of Asthma Remediation
        services. The initial visit must identify member/caregiver knowledge, skills, and needs related to asthma,
        determine asthma control status by administrating and scoring a validated, age-appropriate asthma
        control Screening questionnaire (ACT, C-ACT, TRACK), and identify and provide education on home
        environmental factors/triggers potentially impacting asthma

        o   For the remainder of this Waiver period, if an ASME provider cannot be identified to conduct the
            Initial Visit in-person, the visit may be conducted virtually face-to-face (e.g., video call).

    •   Final Visit: may be conducted in-person in the member’s dwelling or face-to-face virtually (e.g., video
        call) and must be no earlier than 45 days post completion of all Asthma Remediation services. In the rare
        circumstance where the member does not allow a final face-to-face visit in-person or virtually, the final
        visit may be conducted telephonically. The final visit must include asthma and home environmental
        post-assessments, administration and scoring of a validated age-appropriate asthma control Screening
        questionnaire (ACT, C-ACT, TRACK) to determine changes in asthma control status, reinforcement of
        ASME education, and reporting on member’s progress and improvements in the home environment
[[p.172]]
The Social Care Navigator should make referrals if necessary for the member or their family if applicable before
the Asthma Remediation service duration period ends.
Dwelling Assessment & Scope of Work (SOW) Development (including SOW Technical Review) (part of 2.3b):
    •   Dwelling Assessment & SOW Development: A comprehensive dwelling assessment of the primary
        residence to identify Home Remediations needed to reduce or eliminate asthma triggers and improve
        the indoor environment of the dwelling. Assessment should be conducted by a qualified home
        improvement contractor with industry-standard credentials in building science and healthy homes
        principles and incorporate results and relevant environmental findings from the initial ASME visit. The
        SOW should outline recommended remediation services, supportive products, and associated pricing
        based on the assessment. Both the HRSN service provider and contractors’ coordination and
        administrative costs should be included in the SOW and should not exceed 10% of the total costs of the
        project.
    •   SOW Technical Review: Each SOW Technical Review must be conducted by a qualified reviewer with
        industry-standard credentials in building science and healthy homes principles working independently of
        the HRSN service provider for component c. “Home Remediation and Provision of Supportive Products”.
        The SOW Technical Reviewer should ensure clear indication within the SOW when recommended
        services are considered to be invasive and return the SOW to Social Care Navigator. If the SOW includes
        invasive measures, written approval from the property owner (landlord in case of a rental) is required
        before beginning work (approval must be obtained by either the Social Care Navigator or provider of
        component c. Home Remediation and Provision of Supportive Products).
2.3b Asthma Remediation and Supportive Products: Installation services and supportive products may address
ventilation and air quality, removal of asthma triggers, and Integrated Pest Management (IPM). Remediation
services and supportive products will be limited to those listed in the table below and which are recommended
in the SOW and approved by the Social Care Navigator after component b.2 SOW Technical Review. Member
written approval is required to begin installation of approved SOW services. Remediation service providers must
provide proof of credentials/licensure/industry-accepted certifications and training (including advanced
requirements for specialized services such as HVAC, IPM, mold remediation etc.) AND have experience
identifying and remediating asthma-related home environmental triggers. Total costs of services for Asthma
Remediation may not exceed per member cap listed in the HRSN Fee Schedule for duration of Waiver period.
QA Inspection: Within 90 days of service completion, a QA Inspection should be conducted in alignment with
Building Performance Institute (BPI) and other industry technical standards for QA for a minimum of 10 percent
of households where Asthma Remediation services are provided by the SCN. QA provider should be
independent of provider of component c. Home Remediation and Provision of Supportive Products. If a QA
Inspection identifies any issues with the work completed, the Social Care Navigator should work with the HRSN
service provider to ensure work passes the QA Inspection.

                        8. The ASME provider may need to provide additional education to the member in-
                        between Initial visit and Final visit. This time must be billed under the 24 units cap for
                        ASME Home Visits.

 Allowable Providers    1. Contracted Asthma Remediation service providers that are designated as a non-
                        profit community-based organization 501 (c)(3) or 501(c)(4).
                        2. Asthma Remediation services may be performed by a contracted for-profit
                        organization at the SCN Lead Entity’s discretion in absence of an available 501(c)(3) or
                        501(c)(4) community-based organization. See HRSN Network Capacity and Access
                        section for details.
                        3. Asthma Self-Management Education (ASME) must be provided by a qualified
                        nonphysician health care professional, such as a certified asthma educator specialist
                        (AE-C), respiratory therapist (RT), or specially trained lay health worker (e.g., health
                        educator, community health worker (CHW), etc.), with documented training and
                        demonstrated competency in delivering guidelines-based Asthma Self-Management
                        Education and comprehensive home environmental assessments to identify and
                        provide education on reducing asthma triggers.
                        4. Asthma Remediation that is a physical adaptation to a residence must be
                        performed by an individual holding a New York State Contractor’s License.
                        5. IPM services which include pesticide application must be delivered by professionals
                        licensed by the NYS Department of Environmental Conservation.
                        6. HRSN service providers completing Asthma Remediation Services must have proof
                        of credentials/licensure/industry-accepted certifications and trainings AND
                        demonstrated experience providing Home Modifications Component b.1 Dwelling
                        Assessment and SOW Development must be conducted by a qualified home
                        improvement contractor with proof of industry-standard credentials in building
                        science and healthy homes principles.
                        7. Component b.2 SOW Technical Review and component d. QA Inspection must be
                        conducted by a qualified reviewer/inspector holding industry-standard credentials in
                        building science and healthy homes principles working independently of the HRSN
                        service provider for component c. “Home Remediation and Provision of Supportive
                        Products”.
                        8. HRSN service providers offering component c. Home Remediation and Provision of
                        Supportive Products must have proof of credentials/licensure/industry-accepted
                        certifications and trainings (including advanced requirements for specialized services
[[p.176]]
 Asthma Remediation: Eligibility and service details

                         such as HVAC, IPA, mold remediation, etc.) AND demonstrated experience providing
                         home installation improvement services including identifying and remediating
                         asthma-related home environmental triggers.
                         9. HRSN service providers must consult with the member’s locality for any required
                         permits prior to beginning invasive measures listed within the SOW

Workflow for Asthma Remediation Services: The SCN Lead Entity will need to create a unique workflow for
Asthma Remediation services given the multiple service components of Asthma Self-Management Education,
dwelling assessment, and associated Statement of Work (SOW) requirements, Home Remediation and Provision
of Supportive Products, and QA Inspections. Note: Members that are eligible for referral to 2.3 Asthma
Remediation automatically qualify to receive referral for 2.2a Home Remediation Services: Mold and Pest
Remediation and 2.2b Home Remediation Services: Ventilation Improving Systems without a provider
attestation.
In general, the workflow should follow the below steps (see Figure 5-8 for a visual process flow):
    1. If the member is eligible for 2.3 Asthma Remediation services (and therefore automatically 2.2.a and
       2.2.b), the Social Care Navigator will refer to an ASME provider to complete Asthma Remediation
       component a.
    2. The ASME provider (component a.) will contact the member to schedule the initial ASME visit. After
       completion of the initial ASME visit under component a., the ASME provider will report the
       recommended Enhanced HRSN services back to the Social Care Navigator and update the SCN IT
       Platform demonstrating the initial ASME services have been completed.
    3. The Social Care Navigator reviews the HRSN service provider’s findings and recommendations and
       confirms completion of initial ASME visit criteria. The Social Care Navigator then proceeds with securing
       a HRSN service provider to conduct component b.1.
    4. The HRSN service provider for component b.1 will conduct the Dwelling Assessment and SOW
       Development and provide the SOW to the Social Care Navigator via the IT Platform. Only one Dwelling
       Assessment and SOW is required. The provider that conducts the Dwelling Assessment and develops the
       SOW can be reimbursed for admin time, including travel.
    5. The Social Care Navigator will submit the SOW for Technical Review (component b.2.) to a qualified
       reviewer holding industry-standard credentials in building science and healthy homes principles working
       independently of the HRSN service provider for component c. Home Remediation and Provision of
       Supportive Products.
    6. The provider for b.2 conducts the SOW Technical Review, indicates within the SOW which services
       involve invasive measures, and returns the SOW to the Social Care Navigator.
    7. The Social Care Navigator conducts a review of the SOW to ensure all proposed measures are allowable
       since the HRSN service provider may recommend services that are not covered under the Enhanced
       HRSN Services. The total cost for Asthma Remediation services must be at or below the allowable cap
       amount in the HRSN fee schedule. If above the allowable cap, Social Care Navigator must in consultation
[[p.177]]
        with the Technical Reviewer (component b.2), prioritize the appropriate services to authorize for the
        member. The Social Care Navigator must enter and create unique referrals for each service included in
        the approved SOW and document authorized services within the Social Care Plan.
    8. The Social Care Navigator must ensure member written approval of approved SOW services to begin
       remediation services. Any SOW involving invasive measures, as confirmed by the SOW Technical review,
       also requires written approval from the property owner (landlord if the residence is rented).
    9. The Social Care Navigator makes referral to HRSN service provider for component c. Remediation service
       providers for component c. and/or their subcontractors must provide proof of
       credentials/licensure/industry-accepted certifications and training (including advanced requirements for
       specialized services such as HVAC, IPM, etc.) AND have experience identifying and remediating asthma-
       related home environmental triggers. The HRSN service provider or subcontractor of component c.
       proceeds with completing Home Remediation and Provision of Supportive Products as approved in the
       SOW. The HRSN service provider for component c. Home Remediation and Provision of Supportive
       Products may be the same or different entity for component b.1. Dwelling Assessment & SOW
       Development.
    10. Provider of component c. completes Home Remediation Service and Provision of Supportive Products.
    11. For a minimum of 10 percent of households where Asthma Remediation services are provided (as
        determined at the discretion of the SCN Lead Entity), component d. QA Inspection should be conducted
        by a qualified inspector holding industry-standard credentials in building science and healthy homes
        principles, within 90 days of completion of component c. Provider of component d. Quality Assurance
        (QA) Inspection must be independent of the HRSN service provider for component c. Home Remediation
        and Provision of Supportive Products. If a QA Inspection identifies any issues with the work completed,
        the Social Care Navigator should work with the HRSN service provider to ensure work passes the QA
        Inspection.
    12. The HRSN service provider of component c. updates the SCN IT Platform to demonstrate the services
        have been completed. The Social Care Navigator notifies the ASME provider (component a.) of the
        completion of services under component c.
    13. The ASME provider (component a.), follows up with the member to schedule and conduct the final
        ASME visit 45 days after Asthma Remediation services have been completed. The ASME provider
        updates the SCN IT Platform to demonstrate the final services under component a. have been
        completed.
    14. The Social Care Navigator documents the completed services within the Social Care Plan and follows up
        with the member within 5 business days to document their satisfaction.
Note: If the cost of services is $2,000 or more, the HRSN service provider must either:
    a. Obtain at least three bids for any total work of $2,000 or more and select the lowest price and best
       value or substantially equivalent bid, if applicable. As a last resort, the SCN Lead Entity may move
       forward with only two bids if there is limited capacity within SCN region.
    b. If preferred, the SCN Lead Entity can establish a list of preferred contractors through a competitive
       bidding process to be updated annually, and the HRSN service provider can select a contractor for
       recommended modifications from this list without soliciting at least 3 bids for each service.
[[p.178]]
Across both options, bid development (e.g., time spent traveling to the site, writing up the bid) will not be
reimbursed.

Enhanced HRSN Services. SCN Lead Entity may authorize ONLY the approved Enhanced HRSN Services

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.4 Recuperative Care (Medical Respite)
sections.text:
2.4 Recuperative Care (Medical Respite)
Recuperative Care (Medical Respite) is temporary residential care and supportive services provided to homeless
or unstably housed members who do not have an acute need to be hospitalized but require health care services
and supports to continue to recover from an illness or prepare for a medical procedure. Services include short-
term residential care that allow homeless individuals the opportunity to rest in a safe environment while
accessing medical care and other supportive services. Recuperative Care will be provided in the form of short-
term pre-procedure and post-hospitalization service by NYS-certified Medical Respite Programs (MRPs) and in
accordance with New York State’s established Medical Respite regulations (10 NYCRR Part 1007) and program
guidance. Post-hospitalization stay is available for up to 90 days per year (assessed on a rolling basis). Pre-
procedural care is based on the provider’s directions but cannot exceed 30 days per year. Certified MRPs must
also offer transitional supports to help members secure stable housing and avoid future hospital readmissions,
coordinate with the SCN Lead Entity to offer additional Enhanced HRSN Services to the member when
applicable, such as transitional Housing Navigation services, Nutrition supports, Transportation, and Care
Management services prior to the member’s discharge date from the Medical Respite. For further information
about NYS-certified Medical Respite Programs (MRPs) please visit:
https://www.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/redesign/sdh/respite.htm

Recuperative Care may be used as:
[[p.179]]
    a. Short-term Post-Hospitalization Care: provided to eligible members transitioning out of institutions or
       acute care hospitals in which a Social Care Navigator may also consider this population eligible under
       Medicaid High Utilizer, and who are at-risk for incurring other Medicaid state plan service costs, such as
       for inpatient hospitalizations or Emergency Department visits to receive treatment on a short-term
       basis. Need for short term post-hospital care must be indicated in the member’s facility discharge and
       MR referral documents. Following an Eligibility Assessment, the Social Care Navigator will determine
       whether the member meets social and clinical criteria for the service.
    b. Short-term Pre-Procedure Care: provided to eligible members that are experiencing homelessness and
       are scheduled for a medical procedure or surgery that has been indicated as needing preparation or pre-
       surgical care by a medical professional. Referral should document the need for pre-procedure care and
       the anticipated length of stay.

Table 5-27: Recuperative Care (Medical Respite): Eligibility and service details

 Recuperative Care (Medical Respite): Eligibility and service details
 Eligibility              1. Meets at least one of the Enhanced Population criteria for Enhanced HRSN Services
                          in Table 5-13 and Social Risk Factors in Table 5-14, including meeting the HUD
                          definition of homeless or at-risk of homelessness, and
                          2. Meets the clinical criteria in Table 5-15 (as indicated in the referral package or via
                          provider attestation).

 Service Limitations      1. Individual must be assessed for Medical Respite program eligibility and
 and Restrictions         appropriateness in accordance with MR regulations and guidance
                          2. Post-Hospitalization Recuperative Care may be offered for up to ninety (90) days in
                          duration once every 12 months (assessed on a rolling basis)
                          3. Pre-procedure stays are limited to a clinically appropriate amount of time as
                          determined by medical professional but cannot exceed 30 days per year.
                          4. Eligible settings for Recuperative Care (i.e., short-term Pre-Procedure and Post-
                          Hospitalization) must have staffing sufficient in number and qualification to render all
                          required Medical Respite services in accordance with the NYS established Medical
                          Respite regulations (10 NYCRR Part 1007) and relevant program guidance
 Allowable Providers      1. State-certified Medical Respite providers who are contracted with the SCN Lead
                          Entity

Workflow for Medical Respite Service: The SCN Lead Entity will need to create a unique workflow for the
contracted Medical Respite provider due to the requirements that (1) the member will first have an Eligibility
Assessment with the Social Care Navigator and (2) the eligible member will have a secondary assessment
conducted by the Medical Respite facility in accordance with their regulatory requirements (see Figure 5-9 for a
visual process flow). Medical Respites will have the option available to have unique user roles to complete
additional Social Care Navigator responsibilities (e.g., Screening, Navigation, Eligibility Assessment), but they are
not required to.
[[p.180]]
   1. Hospitals, clinics, HRSN service providers, and ecosystem partners will send the member’s referral for
      Medical Respite Program (MRP) services directly to the regional SCN Lead Entity, without HRSN
      Screening or Eligibility Assessment (See below for elements that must be included in this referral)
   2. Social Care Navigators should prioritize MRP referrals and strive for a rapid turnaround of 2 business
      days to outreach the member to complete Screening and Eligibility Assessment. The Social Care
      Navigator will conduct Screening and Eligibility Assessment with the member (if not already completed
      by the referring entity). The clinical criteria required per NYHER can be sourced from the referring
      entity’s referral package.
   3. Based on the Social Care Navigator’s Eligibility Assessment, the SCN’s Social Care Navigator will either:
          a. Reject the referral
               If the Social Care Navigator determines the member is not NYHER eligible after the Eligibility
               Assessment, they will directly inform the member or authorized representative live. The SCN IT
               Platform will have the ability to record the rejection as from the Social Care Navigator. The
               Social Care Navigator will notify the referring entity of the rejection OR;
          b. Accept the referral
               If the Social Care Navigator determines the member meets NYHER eligibility criteria, they will
               directly inform the member or authorized representative live. The Social Care Navigator will
               then refer the member to a local contracted MRP for their regulatory assessment (For timing
               requirements, see HRSN capacity and access guidelines and requirements.)
   4. The MRP will then conduct their regulatory assessment which may be in person in accordance with the
      NYS established regulations and MRP guidance. The MRP will work towards accepting the referral within
      the number of days listed in Section ii. HRSN capacity and access guidelines and requirements. Based on
      the MRP regulatory assessment, the MRP will either:
          a. Reject the SCN’s referral. If the MRP rejects the Social Care Navigator’s referral in the platform
               (due to capacity, individual is not appropriate for facility, etc.), the Social Care Navigator will
               either initiate a referral to another MRP that may accept the member. When attempts have
               been exhausted, the Social Care Navigator will verbally notify the referring entity and the
               member or their authorized representative of the unsuccessful attempts to find an appropriate
               MRP. The SCN IT Platform will record the rejection as coming from the MRP; OR
          b. Accept the SCN’s referral. If the MRP accepts the member’s referral, the MRP will determine an
               appropriate length of stay. The MRP will proceed with SCN IT Platform requirements to accept
               the Social Care Navigator’s referral request
   5. The Social Care Navigator notifies the referring entity that the MRP accepts the referral
   6. The Social Care Navigator documents the referred MRP services within the member’s Social Care Plan
      which will include start date, service duration, indication of pre- or post-respite stay and pre-determined
      date to follow up with the member on any other recommended Enhanced HRSN services
   7. The MRP reviews and uploads to the SCN IT platform documentation verifying the member’s
      homelessness status, if applicable
   8. The MRP proceeds with rendering their services, documents relevant notes into the SCN Social Care Plan
      including estimated discharge date in the SCN IT Platform
   9. The Social Care Navigator documents the completed services within the Social Care Plan and follows up
      with the member / MRP to document the member’s satisfaction. The SCN will work closely with the
      MRP and offer collaborative assistance with care coordination including additional transitional HRSN
[[p.181]]
        services prior to the discharge date (where the member qualifies for additional Enhanced HRSN
        Services)
    10. The SCN Lead Entity proceeds with issuing reimbursement (from PMPM payments) to the MRP on the
        HRSN fee schedule-based reimbursement basis
    11. The SCN Lead Entity proceeds with issuing a completed Social Care Claim to the MCO for completed
        service (for tracking purposes only)

Medical Respite’s Regulatory Assessment

The referring entity’s (Hospitals, clinics, HRSN service providers, and ecosystem partners) referral package sent
to the Social Care Navigator will be used to support the Medical Respite’s regulatory assessment which is
conducted solely by the Medical Respite provider. The clinical criteria required per NYHER may be sourced from
the referring entity’s referral package. However, only the Medical Respite provider can determine if the member
is appropriate to receive Medical Respite services and will not be assessed by the Social Care Navigator.

Referral Package

 A referral from an originating entity (e.g., hospitals, clinics, etc.) to the SCN Lead Entity must include all of the
following:
Basic demographic and identifying information, such as:
       1. Name;
       2. Date of birth;
       3. Social security number (if available);
       4. Copies of any available government-issued documentation (such as driver’s license, non-driver ID, or
            immigration papers); and
       5. Health coverage status (including a copy of any pending application for coverage, if applicable).
       6. Indication of NYHER Eligibility for Medical Respite:
             • Homelessness or at-risk of homelessness
             • Pre-procedure:
                    o Requiring pre-surgical or pre-procedure care as indicated by a medical professional and
                         recommended length of stay, or
             • Post-hospitalization:
                    o Transitioning from an institution or acute care hospitalization related to a health
                         condition or illness, and
                    o Requiring recuperation and care for an illness or injury, and
                    o At-risk for incurring other Medicaid state plan services, such as inpatient hospitalization
                         or Emergency Department visits

NOTE: Medical orders and medical records should be coordinated between referring entity and the Medical
Respite directly, as SCNs may not receive such documentation.
[[p.182]]
Medical orders (coming from original referring entity, not the SCN) for items that the individual will need for
recuperation, such as:
    • 30-day supply of medication(s), either by submitting prescription(s) to a pharmacy or arranging to
       transfer the medication(s) with the recipient;
    • Home health care service orders (if applicable); and
    • Durable medical equipment or other supplies (if applicable).

Medical records that address:
  • The individual’s diagnosis;
  • Pertinent medical history;
  • Results of diagnostic tests or Screenings; and
  • Current or recommended interventions, including post-acute care and medications

The referring entity’s referral package may be communicated in the form of medical records and/or narrative
explanations, and/or a referral form and must include all of the following:
    • Information to support the provider’s conclusion that the individual is experiencing homelessness or at-
        risk of homelessness, including the individual’s current living situation or situation prior to being
        admitted to a facility;
    • Description of the individual’s physical limitations, if applicable, and any reasonable accommodations
        that may be required of the Medical Respite program;
    • Confirmation that the individual can perform ADLs with no or minimal assistance or provision of a
        physician order for certified home health agency services;
    • Confirmation that the individual is self-directing or receives at least part-time supervision from a self-
        directing individual or entity that is responsible for making decisions related to the individual’s ADLs;
    • Confirmation that the individual is not, at the time of referral, a threat of harm to their self or others
[[p.183]]
Figure 5-9: Process flow for Medical Respite services

1

to receive Medical Respite services and c) Medical orders and medical records

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.5 Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back Rent)
sections.text:
2.5 Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back Rent)
Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back Rent) includes payment for rent for up to six months.
Payment for Housing services (e.g., rent payments) must not be paid directly to a member. The SCN must
identify the Housing provider (e.g., HRSN service provider, housing management agency, landlord) to receive
rent payments and coordinate directly with them. Rental subsidy can only be paid to the landlord listed on the
lease or TCO. Rental Subsidy and Back Rent may be used for a. Permanent / Long Term Housing or b. Temporary
/ Transitional Housing.
a. Permanent/Long-Term Housing includes: rent payments for apartments, single room occupancy (SRO) units,
single-family homes, multi-family homes, mobile home communities, accessory dwelling units (ADUs), co-
housing communities, middle housing types, trailers, manufactured homes, manufactured home lots, or motel
or hotel when it is serving as the member’s primary residence (back rent only).
    •   If a member is experiencing IPV in their household, is homeless or at-risk of homelessness and is part of
        the Enhanced Population, then Social Care Navigators can permit reimbursement (towards the 6-month
        service duration) for a member to stay in a motel/hotel as a temporary solution. For this service to be
        successful, the Social Care Navigator must ensure there is a plan in place with the member and housing
        provider to begin efforts towards permanent, long-term housing or transitional housing programs
        through utilization of 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services and/or 2.10 Housing
        Transition and Navigation Services. Back rent can be used when a member meets the HUD definition of
        homeless or at-risk of homelessness (Table 5-14). Eligible costs include rental payments up to the U.S.
        Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Fair Market Rate (past-due or forward rent,
        landlord-paid utilities that are part of the rent payment and not duplicative of other HRSN utility
        payments).
[[p.184]]
b. Temporary/Transitional Housing includes: transitional and recovery housing including bridge, site-based,
population-specific, and community living programs that may or may not offer supportive services and
programming.
For the coordination of the Rent / Temporary Housing service, members should also be referred to one of the
following Enhanced HRSN services: 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing
Transition and Navigation Services. The services of 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services and
2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services include both member and non-member facing coordination and
can be billed as follows:
    1. HRSN service providers’ housing service coordination time should be billed under the applicable 2.7 Pre-
    Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services.
    2. Coordination can also be covered under Enhanced Care Management if the coordination is performed by
    a Social Care Navigator and reimbursement requirements set forth in Section 5.C.ii Reimbursement for
    Social Care Navigation are met.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.6 Utility Setup / Assistance
sections.text:
2.6 Utility Setup / Assistance
Utility Setup / Assistance is limited to members receiving Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back
Rent) service per Section 2.5: Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back Rent) above. Qualified
members may be eligible for assistance with setting up utility services in their new community living setting.
Utility Setup / Assistance services may include one-time activation costs, back payments to secure utilities, and
payment of up to six (6) months of utility costs.
This service provides payment for recurring utilities costs for up to six (6) months. Eligible members may receive
a one-time payment assistance with utility activation fees and/or back payment up to a capped amount, as listed
in the HRSN Fee Schedule. Payment for utility services should not be paid directly to a member. The SCN should
provide payment to the utility provider (e.g., electric company, internet provider, recycling service) directly. This
service will cover expenses for the following types of utility payments:
    •   Garbage
    •   Water
    •   Sewage
    •   Recycling
    •   Gas/oil
[[p.186]]
    •    Electric
    •    Internet
    •    Phone (inclusive of landline phone service and cell phone service)
For the coordination of the Utility Setup / Activation service, members should be referred to one of the
following Enhanced HRSN services: 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing
Transition and Navigation Services. HRSN service providers’ housing service coordination time should be billed
under the applicable 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing Transition and
Navigation Services. Coordination can also be covered under Enhanced Care Management if the coordination is
performed by a Social Care Navigator and reimbursement requirements set forth in Section 5.C.ii
Reimbursement for Social Care Navigation are met.
     o    Utility Activation: Provides payment for non-refundable, non-recurring utility set-up costs or restart
          costs if the service has been discontinued.
     o    Utility Back Payments: Provides one-time payment, up to a capped amount, for utility back payments
     o    Utility Assistance: Covers up to 6 months of utility costs
Table 5-29: Utility Setup / Assistance: Eligibility and service details

                          in Table 5-13 and Social Risk Factors in Table 5-14, including meeting the HUD

                          2. Meets the clinical criteria in Table 5-15
                          3. Must be receiving Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and Back Rent)
                          services as described in Section 2.5 on Rent / Temporary Housing (Rental Subsidy and

 and Restrictions         2. Utility activation fees and/or back payment is limited to a one-time payment

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services
sections.text:
2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services
Under this service, Social Care Navigators can help determine sustainable housing options based on a member’s
eligibility and work with the member towards securing an approved housing application. Once a housing
application is approved, the Social Care Navigator can explore rent or back payments under 2.5 Rent/Temporary
Housing. Medicaid Managed Care members may qualify for Pre-Tenancy Services under this 1115 Waiver
authority, for up to 6 months. These services include:
    •    Assistance with navigating the complexities of the housing application and supporting the member
         when undergoing tenant Screening, completing rental applications, negotiating lease agreements, and
         preparing for and attending tenant interviews
    •    Assistance with the housing search and application process, including contacting prospective housing
         options for availability and information, as well as researching the availability of rental assistance

Members with approved housing applications should also be referred to the following Enhanced HRSN services:
2.5 Rent/Temporary Housing, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services and 2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation
Services.
The services of 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services and 2.10 Housing Transition and
Navigation Services include both member and non-member facing coordination and can be billed as follows:
    1. HRSN service providers’ housing service coordination time should be billed under the applicable 2.7 Pre-
    Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services.
    2. Coordination can also be covered under Enhanced Care Management if the coordination is performed by
    a Social Care Navigator and reimbursement requirements set forth in Section 5.C.ii Reimbursement for
    Social Care Navigation are met.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.8 Community Transitional Supports (CTS)
sections.text:
2.8 Community Transitional Supports (CTS)
Services are intended to assist members who have secured a new housing unit to have a smooth and seamless
transition to community living. Member must be assessed and their need for any of the following services
should be documented in the Social Care Plan. Assistance with the set-up of the new housing unit and review of
the living environment to ensure that it meets the member’s clinical, furnishings, adaptive aids, environmental
modifications, and food and clothing needs at transition. Total costs of services may not exceed per member cap
listed in the HRSN fee schedule for duration of Waiver period. The following one-time transition and moving
costs are included:
   •   Security deposit and brokerage fees;
   •   Utility activation fees, movers, and relocation expenses;
   •   Pest eradication and inspection fees;
   •   Pantry stocking food (limited to a maximum of 30 days of food); and
   •   The purchase of household goods and furniture. Covered furnishings are limited to:
         a. Living Room
             ▪ Couch/ loveseat/ recliner
             ▪ Table
             ▪ Lamp
         b. Kitchen
             ▪ Table and chairs
             ▪ Countertop microwave
             ▪ Garbage pail
             ▪ Kitchen kit: pots, pans, utensils, dishes, dish soap, dishtowels
             ▪ Coffee Pot
             ▪ Toaster (not oven)
         c. Bathroom
[[p.189]]
               ▪   Bathroom kit: bath towels, wash cloths, hand towels, mats for floor and bathtub, basic
                   toiletries including toothbrush, hairbrush or comb, and initial purchase of soap, shampoo,
                   conditioner, toothpaste, and toilet paper
                ▪ Toilet plunger
                ▪ Tension rod
                ▪ Shower curtain, liner, and rings
                ▪ Grab bar
                ▪ Handheld shower head
            d. Other
                ▪ Secure medicine storage container
                ▪ Vacuum under $100
                ▪ Essential cleaning supplies
                ▪ Clock
                ▪ Blinds/ curtains
                ▪ Foldable shopping cart
            e. Bedroom (per participant)
                ▪ Sheets and pillows
                ▪ Waterproof/vinyl mattress and pillow protector
                ▪ Bed (i.e., mattress, box spring, and frame; twin or full size)
                ▪ Comforter
                ▪ Chest of drawers
                ▪ Nightstand
                ▪ Lamp

It is the responsibility of the HRSN service provider to obtain receipts for ALL items purchased. Copies of receipts
must be submitted to the SCN. For provision of security deposits, the HRSN provider should pay the security
deposit directly to the landlord and follow the typical workflow for generating a claim.

For the coordination of the Community Transitional Supports service, members should be referred to one of the
following Enhanced HRSN services: 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing
Transition and Navigation Services. HRSN service providers’ housing service coordination time should be billed

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services
sections.text:
2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services
Medicaid Managed Care members may qualify for a range of services to assist in maintaining and sustaining
their tenancy in affordable or supportive housing by providing tenant rights education and eviction prevention.
Tenancy Sustaining Services are intended to assist members in securing housing and have a smooth and
seamless transition to community living. Service is limited to 6 months, and members must be assessed and
their need for any of the following services must be documented in the service plan. Under this Waiver
authority, Tenancy Sustaining Services will include:
    •   Assistance in linking to free or affordable legal services for members facing housing-related issues;
    •   Connection to available resources to assist in establishing a bank account and paying bills;
    •   Assistance in connecting the member with social services to assist with filling out applications and
        appropriate documentation to obtain sources of income necessary for community living, establishing
        credit, and in understanding and meeting the obligations of tenancy;
    •   Assistance in addressing circumstances and/or behaviors that may jeopardize housing. This should
        include direct interventions to address risks and connect the member to relevant community resources
        that may offer assistance;
[[p.191]]
    •    Assistance in resolving disputes with landlords and/or neighbors to reduce risk of eviction or other
         adverse actions; and
    •    Assistance with housing recertification processes, including lease renewals and housing subsidy
         renewals
The services of 2.7 Pre-Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services and 2.10 Housing Transition and
Navigation Services include both member and non-member facing coordination and can be billed as follows:
    1. HRSN service providers’ housing service coordination time should be billed under the applicable 2.7 Pre-
    Tenancy Services, 2.9 Tenancy Sustaining Services or 2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services.
    2. Coordination can also be covered under Enhanced Care Management if the coordination is performed by
    a Social Care Navigator and reimbursement requirements set forth in Section 5.C.ii Reimbursement for
    Social Care Navigation are met.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services
sections.text:
2.10 Housing Transition and Navigation Services
Medicaid Managed Care members may qualify for assistance navigating and transitioning into a new home, for 4
hours per month for up to 6 months and may be re-authorized up to 6 months per re-authorization, up to the
duration of the Waiver as long as the member has an unmet need and is eligible to receive services. As a guiding
principle, services are not intended to be permanent solutions, and Social Care Navigators should work to
connect members to more permanent resources (existing federal, state, and local services) where possible.
Under this 1115 Waiver authority, Housing Transition and Navigation Services will include:
[[p.192]]
    •    Assistance with the set-up of a new housing unit, including clinically appropriate residential
         modifications, and identifying needs for assistance with arranging the move and supporting the details
         of the move, as appropriate;
    •    Connection to resources aiding with housing costs and other expenses; including linkages to rental
         assistance vouchers, security deposits, application fees, moving costs, etc.;
    •    Review of the living environment to ensure that it meets the clinical needs of the individual and is ready
         for move-in, including collaborating with the relevant provider staff where the individual is
         institutionalized (e.g., hospital or facility social worker) to ensure a seamless transition to the
         community

3. Nutrition
The NYS 1115 Waiver makes available several nutrition support services to meet the eligible Medicaid Managed
Care member’s needs. These nutrition supports are intended to provide timely access to adequate food
resources that provide nourishment and help prevent adverse health and social impacts. All individuals at the
end of the Enhanced HRSN Service duration will also be offered connection to WIC (DOH), SNAP (OTDA), and/or
Older Americans Act nutrition services through Care Management services.
If a member is eligible for Nutrition service re-authorization as described in Section 5. Care Delivery Approach,
part e. Service Re-Authorization, then the member may elect to receive a different type of Nutrition service for
their 6-month reauthorization period if eligible and requested. For instance, a member may have received 6
[[p.193]]
months of Medically Tailored Meals and upon reauthorization, decide to opt for Pantry Stocking. However, if a
member requests to change their Nutrition service in the middle of service period and before re-authorization,
then the sum of the service duration already received must be subtracted from the max service duration
allowed to determine the end date of the new Nutrition service
MLTCP and MAP members are not eligible for 1115 Waiver Nutrition services since they are provided as a plan
benefit with the exception of Cooking Supplies.

Pregnant, postpartum individuals and high-risk children under 18 are eligible for additional MMC members
within their household to also receive Nutrition supports where indicated.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 3.1 Nutrition Counseling and Education
sections.text:
3.1 Nutrition Counseling and Education
SCNs will provide Nutrition Counseling and Education services, including topics on healthy meal preparation and
connecting the individual with grocery budget resources. Nutrition Counseling and Education will be provided by
Certified Dietitian Nutritionists (CDN) / Registered Dietician Nutritionists (RDN), who will assess a member’s
nutrition needs based on age, activity level, and special circumstances resulting from medical conditions such as
diabetes, high blood pressure, food allergies, and obesity. This assessment will help plan for and direct the
provision of food appropriate for physical and dietary needs, provide tailored nutrition counseling, such as
advice on dietary changes, and plan menus and direct the preparation of food to meet dietary needs. Nutrition
Counseling and Education may include the following examples for individuals or groups:
    •   Assessment of nutritional needs and food patterns (HRSN service provider should ensure the
        assessment in saved within the Social Care Plan);
    •   Planning for and directing the provision of food appropriate for physical and nutritional needs;
    •   Nutrition counseling; and
    •   Meal preparation and grocery shopping education
[[p.194]]
Referrals to Nutrition Counseling and Education and other Nutrition services are independent – Social Care
Navigators may refer members to both Nutrition Counseling and Education and other Nutrition services at the
same time. Nutrition Counseling and Education can be used as a standalone service or can be utilized in
conjunction with other Enhanced HRSN Nutrition supports (e.g., provided as an added support to 3.3 Medically
Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions). Nutrition Counseling and Education is not intended to
be used as a pre-cursor referral to other Nutrition services since assessment and intake is already an aspect of
services 3.2 and 3.3. OHIP expects that referrals to Nutrition Counseling and Education will be appropriate and
beneficial for members receiving other Nutrition services. Social Care Navigators may determine whether these
referrals should be made to the same or different HRSN service provider depending on member needs and the
capabilities of HRSN service providers.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 3.2 Meals (3.2a Medically Tailored Meals; 3.2b Clinically Appropriate Home Delivered Meals)
sections.text:
3.2a Medically Tailored Meals
Home delivered prepared Medically Tailored Meals will be available to Medicaid Managed Care members who
have an identified unmet HRSN for nutrition and meet specific eligibility requirements. Meal plans will be
tailored to the medical needs of the member, approved by a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified
Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN), and designed to improve health outcomes, lower cost of care, and increase member
satisfaction.

Medically Tailored Meal providers must provide qualified individuals with medically appropriate meals designed
to meet all of the member’s medical nutrition requirements. Nutrition counseling must be available to members
receiving medically tailored meals. Medically Tailored Meals benefit is designed to be tailored by
[[p.195]]
a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN) to an individual member with a
chronic condition2 and/or pregnant or postpartum persons and must adhere to standards informed by
established nutrition guidelines, such as the Food is Medicine Coalition (FIMC) MTM nutrition standards, for
specific health conditions and tailored to member’s health condition.

Medically Tailored Meals requires RDN / CDN involvement in two steps:

    1. Initial intake / assessment with the member: The initial member intake / assessment must be approved
       by an RDN or CDN. Any employee of the HRSN service provider may conduct intake with the member, so
       long as an RDN or CDN reviews and signs off.

    2. Oversight and meal plan design: An RDN or CDN must design and approve a member’s medically
       tailored meals in order to ensure meals meet all of the member’s medical nutrition requirements. RDN /
       CDN involvement and design of the meal plan is included in reimbursement rate for services.

MTM providers must have in-house RDN/CDNs to conduct this oversight and provide approvals.

Social Care Navigators should refer members to Nutrition services for the maximum duration and dose of the
service. In general, OHIP expects this maximum duration and dose will be appropriate to address the HRSNs of
most members. However, an HRSN service provider may determine in consultation with the member that a
more limited duration and/or dose are more appropriate for the member's circumstances. The HRSN service
provider should invoice the SCN Lead Entity for the actual quantity of service provided.

3.2b Clinically Appropriate Home Delivered Meals
Home delivered clinically appropriate meals will be available to Medicaid Managed Care members who have an
identified unmet HRSN for nutrition and meet specific eligibility requirements. Meal plans will be approved by a
Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN), and designed to improve health
outcomes, lower cost of care, and increase member satisfaction.
Clinically appropriate meals must provide well-balanced, nutritionally appropriate meals that adhere to
evidence-based nutritional guidelines. Clinically appropriate meals promote health and wellness for enhanced
populations who have an unmet HRSN under the food domain and meet the USDA definition of low food
security but do not have chronic conditions and are not pregnant/postpartum persons. All meals provided must
be approved by a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN) and must
adhere to standards informed by appropriate nutrition guidelines.

Clinically Appropriate Meals requires RDN / CDN involvement in two steps:

    1. Initial intake / assessment with the member: The initial member intake / assessment must be approved
       by an RDN or CDN. Any employee of the HRSN service provider may conduct intake with the member, so
       long as an RDN or CDN reviews and signs off.

    2. Oversight and meal plan design: An RDN or CDN must design and approve a member’s Clinically
       Appropriate Meals in order to ensure meals meet all of the member’s medical nutrition requirements.
       RDN / CDN involvement and design of the meal plan is included in reimbursement rate for services.

To streamline member experience, OHIP recommends that HRSN service providers have in-house RDN/CDNs to
conduct this oversight and provide approvals. HRSN service providers may have RDN/CDN as direct employee or
as a sub-contractor paid directly by HRSN service provider. However, if necessary, HRSN service providers may
use an RDN/CDN centralized and staffed at the SCN Lead Entity for member intake and meal approval. If using
an RDN/CDN centralized at the SCN Lead Entity, HRSN service providers may NOT include time spent by
RDN/CDN when billing for services. SCN Lead Entities may NOT bill for RDN/CDN time as part of services, but
may use infrastructure funds to staff an RDN/CDN.

Social Care Navigators should refer members to Nutrition services for the maximum duration and dose of the

sections.title: HRSN Services — 3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions
sections.text:
3.3 Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions
Medicaid Managed Care members who have an identified unmet HRSN for nutrition and meet eligibility criteria
may be eligible for Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions (dairy, produce, meat,
grains and spices). Qualified members may elect to receive this service either as a nutrition voucher or food
boxes. Meal boxes are approved by a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified Dietitian Nutritionist
(CDN) and designed to improve health outcomes, lower cost of care, and increase member satisfaction.
Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions issued in the form of vouchers or coupons
may only be redeemed at food pharmacies, food pantries, grocery stores, farmer's markets, mobile markets,
and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) subscriptions. Members who opt for food boxes will receive a
weekly delivery of food appropriate for complete weekly meals.
If the member is a pregnant/postpartum person, then the member may receive these services either throughout
their pregnancy and up to 12 months postpartum.
Social Care Navigators may refer eligible members for either food boxes or nutrition vouchers based on each
member’s preference.
HRSN service providers may charge for food, delivery, and administrative costs associated with each member’s
food prescription services. Costs associated with the initial intake / assessment and meal plan design may be
billed under the reimbursement range, if RDN / CDN is in-house (employed directly by HRSN service provider or
sub-contracted). SCN Lead Entities should monitor HRSN service providers’ costs within the reimbursement
range to ensure program efficiency.
Food Boxes: Food boxes curated by an RDN or CDN will include enough delivered items per box to create an
estimated 3 meals a day, 7 days a week (21 meals) with amount of food meeting the recommendations of the
RDN or CDN. Hunger Prevention and Nutrition Assistance Program (HPNAP) may be used as a resource for HRSN
service providers designing this service. Food boxes should follow appropriate nutritional standards.

Nutrition Vouchers: Vouchers developed by an RDN or CDN will have a stated dollar amount to reasonably
cover the cost of preparing 21 nutritious meals per week. RDNs or CDNs must develop and be involved with
ongoing voucher redemption with the member.

Medically Tailored or Nutritionally Appropriate Food Prescriptions requires RDN / CDN involvement in two steps:

    1. Initial intake / assessment with the member: The initial member intake / assessment must be approved
       by an RDN or CDN. Any employee of the HRSN service provider may conduct intake with the member, so
       long as an RDN or CDN reviews and signs off.
[[p.200]]
    2. Oversight and meal plan design: An RDN or CDN must design and approve a member’s Food
       Prescription boxes or vouchers in order to ensure meals meet all of the member’s medical nutrition
       requirements. RDN / CDN involvement and design of the food prescription is included in reimbursement
       rate for services.

To streamline member experience, OHIP recommends that HRSN service providers have in-house RDN/CDNs to
conduct this oversight and provide approvals. HRSN service providers may have RDN/CDN as direct employee or
as a sub-contractor paid directly by HRSN service provider. However, if necessary, HRSN service providers may
use an RDN/CDN centralized and staffed at the SCN Lead Entity for member intake and meal approval. If using
an RDN/CDN centralized at the SCN Lead Entity, HRSN service providers may NOT include time spent by
RDN/CDN when billing for services. SCN Lead Entities may NOT bill for RDN/CDN time as part of services but may
use infrastructure funds to staff an RDN/CDN.

Social Care Navigators should refer members to Nutrition services for the maximum duration and dose of the
service. In general, OHIP expects this maximum duration and dose will be appropriate to address the HRSNs of
most members. However, an HRSN service provider may determine in consultation with the member that a
more limited duration and/or dose are more appropriate for the member's circumstances. The HRSN service
provider should invoice the SCN Lead Entity for the actual quantity of service provided.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 3.4 Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable Groceries (Pantry Stocking)
sections.text:
3.4 Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable Groceries (Pantry Stocking)
Medicaid Managed Care members who have an identified unmet HRSN for nutrition, meet specific population
eligibility criteria, and are deemed eligible during the Eligibility Assessment with SCN may be eligible for pantry
stocking of fresh produce and nonperishable groceries. Pantry Stocking cannot include perishable dairy or meat
items. Provision of this service is limited to high-risk children under age 18 and pregnant/postpartum persons,
for up to six months. Pregnant individuals, as defined in Table 5-13, may receive up to 21 months of fresh
produce and non-perishable groceries (Pantry Stocking).
[[p.202]]
Fresh Produce and Non-Perishable Groceries will serve to nutritionally supplement as estimated 3 meals a day, 7
days a week (21 meals per week). Hunger Prevention and Nutrition Assistance Program (HPNAP) may be used as
a resource for HRSN service providers designing this service. Pantry Stocking will be delivered/picked up to the
member in a weekly box. Pantry Stocking will not include meat or dairy products. OHIP recommends that food
items provided in Pantry Stocking are nutritionally appropriate (e.g., fresh, frozen, canned fruits and vegetables;
canned meats; shelf-stable milk products; plant-based proteins; dried goods; grains; seasonings; spices).
HRSN service providers may charge for food, delivery, and administrative costs associated with each member’s
Pantry Stocking services. SCN Lead Entities should monitor HRSN service providers’ costs within the
reimbursement range to ensure program efficiency.
Social Care Navigators should refer members to Nutrition services for the maximum duration and dose of the
service. In general, OHIP expects this maximum duration and dose will be appropriate to address the HRSNs of
most members. However, an HRSN service provider may determine in consultation with the member that a
more limited duration and/or dose are more appropriate for the member's circumstances. The HRSN service
provider should invoice the SCN Lead Entity for the actual quantity of service provided.

sections.title: HRSN Services — 3.5 Cooking Supplies
sections.text:
3.5 Cooking Supplies
Medicaid Managed Care inclusive of MLTCP and MAP members who have an identified unmet HRSN for
nutrition may qualify for cooking supplies that are necessary for meal preparation and nutritional welfare when
not available through other programs. Service is available up to a capped per member amount, as determined
by each SCN Lead Entity, and can include, but is not limited to:
    •   Kitchenware (e.g., plates, bowls, cooking utensils, mixing bowls, pots and pans, chef’s knife, cutting
        board, eating utensils, silverware, glassware, can opener, colander)
            o   Small appliances to support meal preparation and nutritional welfare (e.g., blender)
    •   Microwave
    •   Full size refrigerator
            o   Social Care Navigators are strongly encouraged to spend no more than $600 per refrigerator.
                The refrigerator listed in this section is independent from the medical mini refrigerator available
                under Service 2.2c Home Remediation
When appropriate, Social Care Navigators may coordinate the purchase of a member's cooking supplies if more
efficient than referring to an HRSN service provider. A Social Care Navigator should refer the member to
service 3.5 Cooking Supplies and accept the referral as the HRSN service provider to deliver the service. After
[[p.204]]
accepting the referral, the Social Care Navigator may complete the purchase. Time spent by Social Care
Navigators on coordination of services (ordering supplies) may be billed to Enhanced Care Management.

For HRSN service providers that are not Social Care Navigators, time spent coordinating the purchase of a
member’s cooking supplies may be billed under the Cooking Supplies service. Reimbursement for Cooking
Supplies is based on actual costs, subject to a per member cap set by SCNs, based on the total SCN-level cap
listed in the HRSN Fee Schedule. HRSN service providers’ coordination costs are capped at 5% of the cost of each
member’s cooking supplies.

4. Transportation

sections.title: HRSN Services — 4.1 Transportation Services
sections.text:
4.1 Transportation Services
Transportation services may be available to eligible Medicaid Managed Care members who have an identified
unmet HRSN and meet the criteria required for Enhanced HRSN Service within Table 5-15.
Table 5-41: Transportation Screening questions

  Transportation Screening questions
[[p.205]]
 1. In the past 12 months, has lack of reliable transportation kept you from medical         •   Yes
 appointments, meetings, work or from getting things needed for daily living?                •   No

Qualified members may receive access to public or private transportation services (e.g., taxi/livery,
rideshare/Transportation Network Company (TNC), public transportation) to utilize Enhanced HRSN Services
and/or care management activities for which they have been referred. The member’s need for Transportation
services must be documented in their Social Care Plan. Payment for Transportation Services should not be paid
directly to a member. The SCN should provide payment to the Transportation provider directly.
Examples of Enhanced HRSN Services include HRSN-related activities such as:
    •   Housing appointments;
    •   Housing court (eviction prevention);
    •   Local Department of Social Services / Vital Records appointments;
    •   Local Department of Motor Vehicles appointments;
    •   Education and support for chronic conditions;
    •   Court, probation, parole, and order of protection-related appointments;
    •   Childcare / Parenting classes; and
    •   Transportation to food pharmacies, farmer's markets, mobile markets, etc.
The Social Care Navigator, who is directly involved in addressing the member's HRSN needs, will determine the
most cost-effective and appropriate mode of transportation to meet the unique needs of each member. If a
Medicaid member uses the public transit system for the activities of daily life, then, in most circumstances,
transportation for the member should be requested at a mode of transportation no higher than that of the
public transit system. Service is available for a maximum duration of 6 months, with possibility of re-
authorization, up to 6 months per re-authorization, up to the duration of the Waiver as long as the member has
an unmet need and is eligible to receive services. As a guiding principle, services are not intended to be
permanent solutions, and Social Care Navigators should work to connect members to more permanent
resources (existing federal, state, and local services) where possible.
Transportation planning is the responsibility of, and can be billed for by, the member’s Social Care Navigator
under Enhanced Care Management or may be conducted by the HRSN service provider and billed under the
Transportation service. Outside of Social Care Navigation, the cost of transport and transportation coordination
(e.g., coordination with rideshare services) can be billed for by the HRSN service provider under the respective
Transportation Services code. OHIP will track spend against the SCN cap for this service, in addition to collecting
encounter data via social care claims. Transportation providers using volunteer drivers should not bill SCN Lead
Entities for volunteers’ time spent transporting members but may bill for other costs associated with providing
HRSN Transportation Services (e.g., gas).
See section d. v. Considerations for children, youth and households under “Additional considerations for
Transportation services” for coverage details on situations when a child or adult rides with a household member
not eligible for Transportation services.

Congestion Pricing
Congestion pricing is in effect in Manhattan, with congestion tolls charged to vehicles driving below 96th street
and additional congestion tolls charged to vehicles driving below 60th street. NYHER funds cannot be used to
pay congestion tolls under any circumstances. SCN Lead entities and contracted transportation providers
should follow the guidance below, which was in effect as of 1/05/2025.
[[p.207]]
Members eligible for Enhanced Transportation Services should be connected with public transportation
wherever possible, and OHIP expects most rides through Manhattan to involve public transportation (e.g., MTA
subway or bus, MTA Access-A-Ride). In certain circumstances, a member eligible for Enhanced Transportation
Services may require a private ride (e.g., taxi or rideshare). OHIP encourages Social Care Navigators to refer
members to services in their communities. However, in some cases, it may be necessary for a member to ride
through the Manhattan Congestion Relief Zone (CRZ) to access a service.
Recommend enrollment in the Per-Trip Charge Plan
All Transportation providers operating in the NYC area and contracted into SCNs are encouraged – but not
required – to enroll in the Per-Trip Charge Plan (PTCP), a program that affords discounted congestion pricing for
for-hire vehicles (FHVs) entering the CRZ. Vehicles registered to organizations enrolled in PTCP will be charged
$0.75 per trip (green/yellow taxis and black cars) or $1.50 per trip (high-volume FHVs) through the CRZ below
60th street, instead of the usual $9 per day congestion toll.
FHV rides that begin in, end in, or pass through the CRZ will be subject to an additional congestion surcharge of
$2.50, if Transportation providers are not enrolled in PTCP. If transportation providers are enrolled in PTCP,
there are no additional fees to rides that originate and end inside the CRZ.
To enroll in PTCP, Transportation providers must first join a Taxi & Limousine Commission (TLC) base.
Enrolling in PTCP is done through the Transportation service provider’s TLC base, which functions as both an
operating and dispatching base for FHVs. TLC bases seeking to enroll their vehicles in PTCP will need to execute
and deliver the PTCP agreement to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA). The PTCP agreement
includes the following:
    •   The organization must enter into the Central Business District (CBD) Tolling Program FHV Base Per-Trip
        Charge FHVB Plan Acceptance Agreement with the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority (TBTA)
    •   Within three business days from the effective date of the agreement, the organization must provide a
        Vehicle Data Report, including vehicle license plate numbers, state that issued the license plates, and
        vehicle types
    •   The organization must ensure the accurate collection of the CBD FHV Toll Charge for each CBD Trip and
        retain records. Payments must be made monthly within thirty calendar days after the end of each
        month in which a CBD Trip occurred
    •   The organization must implement geofencing or other effective technology to ensure the correct
        application and collection of the CBD FHV Toll Charge for each trip
    •   The organization must maintain records of each CBD Trip and related payments for no less than six years
        after the date of payment
More information on PTCP and how to enroll can be found on the MTA website (see section titled “FHV
enrollment”). Transportation providers contracted with the SCN Lead Entity who meet the criteria to join a TLC
base and PTCP requirements should make every effort to enroll.
Guidance on congestion toll invoicing and reimbursement
Transportation providers who deliver a ride through the CRZ – regardless of their enrollment in PTCP – should
submit a separate invoice to the SCN Lead Entity for the congestion toll paid, distinct from the cost-based
invoice for the rest of the ride. Transportation providers will receive a separate payment for the congestion
pricing portion of the ride than for the rest of the cost of the ride. SCN LEs are required to maintain detailed
documentation on congestion toll invoices submitted from Transportation service providers.
[[p.208]]
For all members receiving Transportation services that involve congestion tolls, SCN Lead Entities will submit
