For Direct Questioning by a Screener (Virtual, or In-Person)

For Screening questions #1-12, the Social Care Navigator may proceed with the Screening even if any of the
questions are left blank. Blank responses should be transmitted to FHIR IG as any DataAbsentReason Code,
recommended to be "Unknown".

For questions #9-12 only, related to Interpersonal Safety, a member can decline to answer, or a Social Care
Navigator may decide not to ask the questions at their own discretion. See, Section 5 part viii. “Considerations
for interpersonal safety questions asked during Screening” for additional Social Care Navigator support.

For Self-Administered Screenings (Website)

It is required that all questions are answered (with the exception of interpersonal safety) or a member will not
be able to submit the Screening.

vi. Eligibility Assessment ICD-10 / SNOMED-CT Coding
All positive AHC HRSN Screening Tool responses will require further Eligibility Assessment. The coding required
during the Eligibility Assessment can only be completed by manual data entry by the Social Care Navigator by
selecting an appropriate ICD-10 and SNOMED-CT description of member’s unmet HRSN. The Eligibility
Assessment finding provided by the Navigator will trigger accurate referral information.

If a member is screened and identified as having an unmet HRSN on any associated individual AHC HRSN
Screening Tool question and during the Eligibility Assessment confirms their desire to accept the HRSN referral, a
[[p.307]]
corresponding ICD-10 Z code (social condition) and SNOMED-CT code (detailed findings associated with
Enhanced HRSN service) will be used to map each identified need.

NOTE: "SNOMED-CT and ICD-10 Z codes will only be used upon a member’s positive Screening result and
confirmation of their unmet HRSN during the one-on-one Eligibility Assessment with the Social Care Navigator.
The condition status should be confirmed during the Assessment."

Eligibility Assessment ICD-10 Z Codes and SNOMED-CT Codes: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability
Guidance on the NYeC website 1115 page for access to up-to-date coding tables on NYeC’s NYHER 1115
Extranet.

For Direct Questioning During Eligibility Assessment (Virtual, or In-Person)

Every data field of the MVD integrated into the Eligibility Assessment must be answered by the member. The
Social Care Navigator should conduct a comprehensive Eligibility Assessment informed by the member’s
identified needs from the HRSN Screening. The Social Care Navigator should answer all relevant questions. If a
member’s only positive Screening outcome was Interpersonal Safety, the Eligibility Assessment ICD10/SNOMED
may be left blank.

vii. Social Care Plan: Person-Centered Goal Setting: SNOMED-CT
Social Care Plans are developed during Eligibility Assessments for members who belong to Enhanced Services
Population(s). The Social Care Plan records member specific care considerations for delivery of HRSN services.
The Social Care Plan is intended to be longitudinal and revisited as services are rendered and needs are met.

Person-Centered Goal Setting codes are available and encouraged to use in Year 1 but are not required to be
used until Year 3.

The goals in the Social Care Plan are the intended objective(s) for the member to address their HRSNs. Goals
may also be directly referenced in a referral by the Social Care Navigator (i.e., FHIR Service Request bundle with
Goal, etc.). The following table outlines the SNOMED Code and the description to enable.

Person-Centered Goal Setting SNOMED-CT Codes: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability Guidance
on the NYeC website 1115 page for access to up-to-date coding tables on NYeC’s NYHER 1115 Extranet.

viii. Navigation & Referrals: SNOMED-CT
Navigation services and referrals to Enhanced HRSN Services are sent upon completion of an Eligibility
Assessment. The corresponding codes will cause a workflow to initiate referrals for relevant HRSN services. The
SCN Lead Entity is responsible for developing a workflow to assign these referrals to a contracted community-
based organization (CBO) within their network. The SCN's Social Care Navigator will have the capability to select
the specific HRSN service provider from within their network for these referrals. It is imperative to meticulously
document all services, including referrals, that are generated based on the SNOMED-CT and ICD-10 codes
assigned during the Navigation and referral process.

Navigation population members are navigated to existing services to meet their HRSNs.
[[p.308]]
Navigation to HRSN related services: SNOMED-CT Codes: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability
Guidance on the NYeC website 1115 page for access to up-to-date coding tables on NYeC’s NYHER 1115
Extranet.

Referral to Enhanced HRSN Services: Care Management SNOMED-CT Codes: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY
Interoperability Guidance on the NYeC website 1115 page for access to up-to-date coding tables on NYeC’s
NYHER 1115 Extranet.

ix. Provision / Interventions HRSN Services: SNOMED-CT
The SCN IT Platform will record provision / interventions to address HRSN provided by the Social Care Network.
The community organization that accepts the referral will provide the service to the member, will coordinate
provision of the service with the member, and record its provision in the SCN IT Platform. SNOMED-CT codes will
be assigned to the interventions recorded in the software and shared with the QE.

Intervention Codes for provision of HRSN services: SNOMED-CT: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY
Interoperability Guidance on the NYeC website 1115 page for access to up-to-date coding tables on NYeC’s
NYHER 1115 Extranet.
New York State has requested updates to the SNOMED-CT codes for HRSN services. SNOMED-CT and other
standards organizations meet every month to review and adopt these proposed changes. Some of the changes
requested by OHIP have already been scheduled for discussion and potential adoption, while others are still
awaiting scheduling.

Proposed Intervention Codes for HRSN services: SNOMED-CT: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability
Guidance on the NYeC website 1115 page for access to up-to-date coding tables on NYeC’s NYHER 1115
Extranet.

To ensure that programmatic needs for referral specificity are met, NYS is currently working with its partners to
seek creation and approval of new SNOMED CT codes. For those situations where referrals do not yet have a
SNOMED CT, the SCN will be directed to use a NYS local code until official coding is released (see anticipated
publication dates below).

x. Billing and Payment Protocol: HCPCS + Modifiers
The SCN IT Platform will generate a unique OHIP-defined HCPCS code and modifier that will be assigned to all
the Enhanced HRSN services for billing purposes as a 1-to-1 coding option. The HRSN service provider who
receives the referral via the SCN IT Platform will have the capability to mark the member’s service as rendered.
SCN Lead Entities will reimburse HRSN service providers in accordance with the OHIP approved HRSN Fee
Schedule for Screening, Navigation, and Enhanced HRSN services delivered. In order for claims to process, the
appropriate HCPCS code and associated modifier must be entered. Note: Modifiers must be entered in the same
order as they appear below.

Billing and Payment: HCPCS and Modifiers: Please refer to the 1115 SHIN-NY Interoperability Guidance on the
NYeC website 1115 page for access to the live documents on NYeC’s NYHER 1115 Extranet.

f. DATA AND SYSTEMS IMPLEMENTATION GUIDE (DSIG)
The NYHER Data and Systems Implementation Guide (DSIG) provides guidance on member enrollment and
population identification, HRSN billing, claims, and data management guidance for the successful
implementation of the NYHER Program. Specifically, the DSIG includes requirements around data transmission
and the specific files that are exchanged between the SCN Lead Entities, their selected IT Platforms, NYeC,
MCOs, QEs, and OHIP.

The DSIG should be referenced by technical staff of SCNs and MCOs involved in implementing and managing the
NYHER program. Please note that two separate DSIGs are available, tailored to the primary audience: SCN Lead
Entities or MCOs. The DSIGs can be accessed by SCN Lead Entities, MCOs, and SCN IT platform vendors on the
NYHER 1115 Extranet site or the NYHER Systems Workgroup SharePoint site.
[[p.310]]

sections.title: OHIP Privacy and Security Requirements — Introduction
sections.text:
a. INTRODUCTION
The SCN Lead Entity’s Data Governance is the collection of policies and procedures that standardize data
management, advance interoperability, and ensure secure distribution of HRSN data. The importance of
safeguarding sensitive information and ensuring regulatory compliance cannot be overstated. Data governance
frameworks ensure that data collected, stored, and shared within the SCN Lead Entity and exchanged between
the SCN Lead Entities and other stakeholders is handled responsibly and securely. Data governance provides the
decision-making processes for the SCN Lead Entity governing body and its appointees to ensure that data is
consistent, complete, interoperable, secure, discoverable, and trustworthy.

Data privacy and security controls and procedures are crucial for the SCN Lead Entity to protect sensitive
member information from being misused or accessed by unauthorized people.

sections.title: OHIP Data Governance Framework
sections.text:
b. DATA GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK

i. Data governance structure
The SCN Lead Entity shall establish decision-making processes for the network across institutional,
administrative, and data governance. Institutional governance sets the framework for participation, leadership
organization, priority setting, rulemaking, outcome evaluation, and conflict resolution. Administrative
governance translates institutional policies into actionable plans, ensuring compliance, information sharing, and
operational standards. Data governance involves implementing and enforcing these policies through meticulous
data stewardship, including managing data collection, storage, exchange, and deletion. Effective governance
ensures that all levels work cohesively to facilitate transparent and accountable decision-making processes.

ii. Data ownership
SCN Lead Entities shall own their data. However, SCN data may only be shared with approved entities for
purposes of meeting SCN programmatic objectives and cannot be shared or used for commercial purposes. Data
is derived or sourced from the Medicaid Program, and this may be provided by the Department directly or
through the QEs / other third-parties. Each element of Medicaid Confidential Data (MCD) is confidential
regardless of the document, mode of communication, or storage in which it is found. Data will not be considered
“Medicaid Data” and owned by OHIP until it reaches New York State’s Medicaid Data Warehouse (MDW).
Health-Related Social Needs (HRSN) data generated through the SCN Lead Entity will be owned by the
[[p.311]]
originating entity until there is a disclosure and/or transmittal from the SHIN-NY to New York State’s Medicaid
program. Once HRSN data generated is transmitted to New York State’s Medicaid program, the data will be
considered owned and governed by OHIP.

iii. Data stewardship and oversight
The SCN Lead Entity shall establish data stewardship processes in compliance with the technical standards, data
collection, management, storage, exchange, verification, validation, contestation, and deletion established by
OHIP.

OHIP will conduct an internal risk-based evaluation of the SCN Lead Entity’s technical and privacy standards
through the DOH System Security Plan (SSP) v5 Critical Controls Attestation Form, System Overview, and
through a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) report. As detailed in section 10.c, OHIP will then employ a
combination of attestations and independent third-party audits to confirm that required security and privacy
controls are in place within the defined system boundary.

sections.title: OHIP Data Privacy and Security
sections.text:
c. DATA PRIVACY AND SECURITY

i. Introduction

SCN Lead Entities’ data privacy and security will be governed by New York State (NYS) Health IT regulations, NYS
Department of Health Office of Health Insurance Programs Division of Operations and Systems (DOS) Security
and Privacy Bureau requirements, and other applicable privacy and security federal and state laws and
regulations.
Federal and state laws protect the confidentiality of Medicaid member data regardless of the document, mode
of communication, or storage in which it is found. This data includes, but is not limited to, Protected Health
Information (PHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII); however, it also includes the following:
•   Names and addresses of Medicaid applicants/recipients
•   Medical services provided
•   Social and economic conditions or circumstances
•   Department of Health evaluation of personal information
•   Medical data, including diagnosis and history of disease or disability
•   Income, eligibility information, and amount of Medicaid payments
•   Information regarding the identification of third parties, and/or information the Department deems to be
    part of the operations of the Medicaid program that is of a sensitive nature, such as cost of services
    provided, and has repercussions if released
Collectively, OHIP refers to these data as Medicaid Confidential Data (MCD). To protect MCD, the Department
has defined a Moderate-Plus Security Controls Baseline based on, and consistent with the security provisions
described in Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Acceptable Risk Safeguards (ARS) and National
Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53 at the Moderate level. Additionally,
the Department has augmented these federal standards with New York State Policies and Standards.
[[p.312]]
Prior to OHIP permitting the release of Medicaid Confidential Data (MCD) to external organizations, those
organizations shall demonstrate compliance with the Moderate-Plus Security and Privacy Controls Baseline to
the Department’s satisfaction.
As the SCN Lead Entity’s digital maturity will evolve over time, it is understood that the SCN Lead Entity will
systematically assess and strengthen its data privacy and security measures as necessary. The use of
independent audits will ensure compliance with applicable federal and state privacy and security laws,
regulations, and consensus adopted standards ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, SOC 1, and SOC 2 standards.

ii. Current State Security Assessment
After the contract was executed, the SCN Lead Entity met with New York State’s Security and Privacy Bureau to
assess the SCN Lead Entity’s current state of security readiness and its IT systems.
OHIP aims to continue to guide SCN Lead Entities through a comprehensive process that will track security and
privacy control adherence to ensure the proper protections are in place.

iii. Annual Privacy and Security Attestation and Audit
SCNs are required to submit annually the Medicaid Critical Controls Attestation which informs DOH of the SCN
Lead Entity’s current security and privacy posture. Periodic independent third-party audits are required. These
third-party audits verify what was attested to in the Medicaid Critical Controls Attestation.

iv. Quarterly POA&M and Quarterly Names List (QNL) Requirements
The following activities must be completed and submitted on a quarterly basis by SCN Lead Entities to support
ongoing oversight and compliance with the Medicaid Data Use Agreement (DUA) and privacy/security protocols:
Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) and Quarterly Names List (QNL).

Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M):

    •   Based on findings from the Medicaid Critical Controls Attestations and the third-party audits, SCN Lead
        Entities must take action to correct any deficiencies identified and add them to the SCN Lead Entity’s
        POA&M report
    •   POA&Ms are required to be submitted to the Security and Privacy Bureau quarterly as well as with an
        annual attestation submission. The POA&M and annual attestation control status must match during the
        submission
    •   POA&Ms are due quarterly even if SCN Lead Entities do not have any updates
    •   Items should not be removed from the POA&M as it is a historical document. The SCN Lead Entity and
        OHIP will monitor progress of control implementation against the POA&M

Quarterly Names List (QNL):

    •   SCN Lead Entities must submit a QNL that documents the name of every individual who accesses
        Medicaid Confidential Data (MCD) – in any way – on the SCN Lead Entity’s behalf. If vendors or
        contractors – including billing contractors – are performing any service, then the Requesting entity shall
[[p.313]]
        include the names of these contractors on the QNL. Such activities may include running analytics or
        hosting data that results in MCD access.

QNL must include:

    •   First and last names
    •   MCD access start and end dates
    •   Email address (usernames are not required)
    •   Company name and address. This should be the company the person works for, not the SCN Lead Entity

Exclusions:

    •   Individuals from state agencies, DOH, and DOH Contractors should not be included on the names list
    •   Exception where the SCN has contracted directly with a third-party for services

v. Medicaid Critical Controls Attestation, System Overview, and Data Use Agreement
The SCN Lead Entity must complete and maintain the OHIP Medicaid Security plan. This plan consists of:
   • Medicaid Critical Controls Attestation and system overview. The original deadline for this was December
       31, 2024, and this is complete.
   • Third-Party Audit and Report - Within one year from acceptance of the attestation the SCN will procure
       an independent third-party auditor to evaluate the controls to which the SCN has attested. This
       evaluation ensures the controls are implemented correctly, are operating as intended, and are
       producing the desired results for any system that is included in the system boundary. The auditor must
       produce a report for the Security and Privacy Bureau detailing the status of each critical control in the
       attestation. The SCN and auditor shall collaborate on the completion of the POA&M such that details of
       the deficiency are recorded along with proposed remediation dates for all controls that have not been
       fully implemented. The annual attestation, audit report, and POA&M must be delivered to the Security
       and Privacy Bureau by December 31, 2025. OHIP asks that SCN Lead Entities submit the annual
       attestation and third-party audit as early as possible in December to allow for processing time. OHIP
       requires the entire report generated by the SCN Lead Entity’s auditor along with the submission of the
       POA&M. SCN Lead Entities should also submit updated System Overview if there are any changes to
       contact information, or other items, listed in the Overview.
   • The SCN is responsible for ensuring that any vendors included in the system boundary meet the same
       controls attested to by the SCN. The SCN/independent auditor shall merge any vendor non-compliant
       controls into the report and POA&M.
   • Medicaid All Controls Attestation - By the end of both years 2026 and 2027, the SCN shall submit an
       updated system overview and attestation to the Security and Privacy Bureau showing the status of each
       control, not only the critical controls, as they did in previous years. In other words, controls previously
       marked as OPTIONAL will now be required. The status of each control in the attestation shall match the
       status of each control listed in the POA&M.
   • Medicaid All Controls Attestation plus Audit – By the end of 2028, the SCN shall obtain another
       independent third-party audit and submit an updated system overview and the annual attestation and
       audit report. The audit shall consist of all controls in the attestation
   • Future Cadence - After 2028, the cadence of deliverables to the Security and Privacy Bureau will be an
       annual attestation each year, with an updated annual attestation and third-party independent audit in
[[p.314]]
        the third year of the cadence. All audits must result in a report submitted to the Security and Privacy
        Bureau.

POA&M submission requirements.

Submission instructions: All Security and Privacy documentation should be emailed to
doh.sm.Medicaid.Data.Exchange@health.ny.gov (Please email your submissions as early as possible within the
month in which each is due.)

Reporting Possible Incidents/Events: SCNs must notify the Security and Privacy Bureau within one hour of the
discovery of an actual or potential security/privacy event or incident. This notification should be made via email
only and does not require a full incident report at that time. This aligns with the Data Use Agreement (DUA),
Section 9, which states:

If DOH determines or believes that the Requestor has used, reused or disclosed MCD in a way other than as
expressly authorized by this Agreement, DOH may require the Requestor to:
a. Promptly investigate and report to DOH the Requestor’s determinations regarding any alleged or actual
    unauthorized use or disclosure;
[[p.315]]
b. Promptly resolve any problems identified by the investigation;
c. Submit a formal response to the allegation of unauthorized use, reuse or disclosure;
d. Submit a corrective action plan with steps designed to prevent any future unauthorized uses, reuses or
   disclosures; and
e. Destroy all data sets received from DOH and submit a Data Destruction Attestation

Additionally, the DUA requires that notification of any incident involving personally identifiable information (PII)
or protected health information (PHI) must also include notifying any unauthorized recipients and affected
individuals, without cost to DOH.

Offshore Access: The DUA prohibits offshore processing, storing, accessing, or transmitting MCD. Specifically,
DUA Section 8: Offshore Prohibition states:
The Requestor agrees that any MCD provided under this Agreement shall not be accessed by employees, agents,
representatives, or contractors/business associates who are located outside of the United States and its
territories (offshore). Further, the Requestor agrees that MCD shall not be received, stored, processed, or
disposed via information technology systems which are located offshore.

Environment Changes: SCNs may not move MCD from any part of an approved environment without first having
a DUA Addendum making the environment change accepted by the Security and Privacy Bureau. Per DUA
Section 6: Data Storage and Access:
When Requestor and Custodian take possession of MCD, it shall be stored in the location specified below. The
data cannot be transferred by any means to another environment without a DUA Addendum to this Agreement
that has been accepted by DOH.
Entities must notify OHIP and the Security and Privacy Bureau if they are considering an environment change,
and they must go through the full approval process prior to making any change.

Environment Changes – Process
    1. The entity notifies the Security and Privacy Bureau of an intent to modify the environment and submits
       an updated system overview document.
    2. The Security team works with the entity to get the system overview and attestation accepted.
           a. Once accepted, the Privacy team provides a DUA addendum, which the entity completes to:
           b. Modify Section 6
    3. Add the third party/downstream partner as a Business Associate by submitting and acknowledging a
       Business Associate Agreement (BAA).
    4. Acceptance of this addendum serves as written permission for the entity to share MCD with the other
       party.

vi. Prohibited Uses
The following uses of SCN Data are prohibited:

    •   The sale of individually identifiable information (including but not limited to PHI and PII);
    •   The use of individually identifiable information for marketing purposes that would require an
        authorization under 45 C.F.R. § 164.508(a)(3); and
    •   Any purpose prohibited by applicable law
[[p.316]]
SCNs must develop breach response plans and promptly notify affected parties and regulatory agencies in the
event of a PHI breach. The SCN must notify the Security and Privacy Bureau and the NYHER program of a
possible event or security breach within 1 hour of identification of indicators of compromise. The Security and
Privacy Bureau shall be notified at doh.sm.Medicaid.Data.Exchange@health.ny.gov and
IncidentReport@health.ny.gov.
[[p.317]]

 Service Description     Medically tailored meals are designed to be tailored by a Registered Dietitian
                         Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN) to an individual member
                         with a chronic condition and/or pregnant or post-partum persons and must adhere to
                         standards informed by established nutrition guidelines, such as the Food is Medicine
                         (FIMC) MTM nutrition standards, for specific health conditions.

                         Clinically appropriate meals must provide well-balanced, nutritionally appropriate
                         meals that adhere to evidence-based nutritional guidelines. Clinically appropriate
                         meals promote health and wellness for enhanced populations who have an unmet
                         HRSN under the food domain and meet the USDA definition of low food security but
                         do not have chronic conditions and are not pregnant/postpartum persons. All meals
                         provided must be approved by a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) or Certified
                         Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN) and must adhere to standards informed by appropriate
                         nutrition guidelines.

e. TRANSPORTATION
Table 11-25: Fee Schedule - Transportation Services: Public & Private

 4.1 Transportation Services: Public & Private

 Service             Provision of Medicaid member-occupied public or private transportation services to
 Description         Enhanced HRSN Services to which they have been referred or other HRSN-related
                     activities. Transportation services may include taxi/livery, rideshare/Transportation
                     network company (TNC), or public transportation.

                     Transportation planning can be billed for by the member’s Social Care Navigator under
                     Enhanced Care Management or may be conducted by the HRSN service provider and
                     billed under the Transportation service.

                     Transportation providers using volunteer drivers should not bill SCN Lead Entities for
                     volunteers’ time spent transporting members but may bill for other costs associated with
                     providing HRSN Transportation services (e.g., gas). Family members of a member
                     receiving Transportation services cannot provide transportation to the member as a
                     volunteer driver for a Transportation service provider.

                        • Private (T2025, U4, U6) or Public (T2025, U3, U6) Transportation to Enhanced

                        • Private (T2025, U7, U6) or Public (T2025, U5, U6) Transportation to HRSN Services
                             Only : Reimbursement for private or public transportation to connect member to
                             HRSN services, such as:
                        • Housing appointments;
                        • Housing court (eviction prevention);
                        • Local Department of Social Services / Vital Records appointments;
                        • Local Department of Motor Vehicles appointments;
                        • Education and support for chronic conditions;
                        • Court, probation, parole, and order of protection-related appointments;
                        • Childcare / Parenting classes; and
                     Transportation to food pharmacies, farmer's markets, mobile markets.
